#1934. Brest vs Lyon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 06 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 20:33

On a mission to record back-to-back wins, Brest welcome title-chasing Lyon to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Sunday afternoon for a Ligue 1 contest.

Les Pirates picked up a comfortable success at Lorient last time out, whereas Les Gones have been busy on continental duty, sharing the spoils at Real Sociedad.

After a mediocre 12th-placed finish in Ligue 1 last season, Brest are aiming to qualify for European competition this time around, with their recent form suggesting that a continental charge could be successful.

Les Pirates have lost just one of their past four top-flight matches after picking up a 2-0 away triumph at Lorient on Monday night, when Ludovic Ajorque and Noah Edjouma found the net in the second half.

Aiming to record consecutive top-flight victories for the first time since early March, Brest are currently occupying 10th position in the Ligue 1 standings, eight points behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain.

Rather surprisingly, only four of Les Pirates' 12 league points have been collected at Stade Francis-Le Ble so far this campaign, with Julien Lachuer's men winning only one of their opening four home contests.

That sole success was impressive and emphatic in equal measure, though, as leading marksman Ajorque provided a goal and an assist in a 5-1 battering of relegation-threatened Angers on October 10.

Following back-to-back wins over Anderlecht and Conference League champions Crystal Palace to commence their Europa League campaign, Lyon have earned just one point from clashes with Hoffenheim (0-3) and Real Sociedad (1-1).

In fact, Les Gones have won just one of their past four matches (D1 L2) across all competitions, with their most recent away league outing ending in a 2-0 victory for PSG at Parc des Princes.

However, Jorge Maciel's troops were able to strengthen their faint title hopes last Sunday afternoon, when goals either side of the half-time break from Ernest Nuamah and Corentin Tolisso were enough to beat Angers.

That success extended their unbeaten home league run to five matches (W4 D1) and moved Lyon up to third position in the Ligue 1 table, just three points behind Luis Enrique's European champions.

Les Gones are unbeaten across their past three encounters (W2 D1) with Brest; however, Les Pirates are unbeaten in the past three meetings (W2 D1) between the sides at Stade Francis-Le Ble.

Brest are expected to be without the services of Brendan Chardonnet, who is sidelined for up to two weeks because of a calf problem.

Les Pirates' options at centre-back are further reduced by the absence of 20-year-old Raphael Le Guen.

A high-profile loanee from Juventus, Lois Openda is currently in the Lyon treatment room because of a leg injury.

With the Belgian set to return after the international break, Nuamah is an important source of goals this weekend for Les Gones.

Wanted by Championship side Wrexham in the summer, Pavel Sulc is out until January with a knee injury.

Selvik; Lala, Tousart, Lloris, Locko; Chotard, Magnetti; Balde, Doumbia, Mboup; Ajorque

Greif; Athekame, Bacher, Niakhate, Abner; Bidstrup, Tessmann, Tolisso; Duranville, Nakamura, Nuamah

After a positive result at Lorient last weekend, Brest face a tougher test in the form of Lyon this time around.

Despite exerting themselves in Spain on Thursday night, Les Gones should be fresh enough to earn a point at Stade Francis-Le Ble.

#1931. Wily veterans and the fountain of youth: The five key battles in Milan vs. Ferencvaros

AC Milan return to Europa League action at San Siro this evening for a must-win game against high-flyers Ferencvaros.

Starting their European campaign with two defeats (vs. Benfica and Bournemouth) and one win last left Milan down in 24th in the table, meaning that they need to turn things around if they are to mount a surge towards the top eight spots.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tonight’s game will be far from straightforward though, as Ferencvaros have taken nine points from nine and therefore sit fourth in the table. They are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and are two points from the summit in their domestic league, with a game in hand to play.

Reports are suggesting that Ruben Amorim will turn to a youthful line-up for this one despite the status of being a must-win game. However, the spine of the team will still be made up of players who must deliver.

Starting with a rather unconventional battle, the one between the two goalkeepers Lorenzo Torriani and Dénes Dibusz could be potentially decisive, for obvious reasons. Ferencvaros have conceded just three goals in their three Europa games so far and just 10 in 10 in the league, and the 35-year-old veteran Dibusz has been a big part of that, even if there has been some rotation.

For Torriani, this is arguably his biggest opportunity in a Milan shirt. His only other start came in a Coppa Italia rout of Sassuolo, while he came off the bench in a Champions League defeat to Liverpool, and in the Bournemouth defeat. This is a huge chance for the 20-year-old to not only show he is a capable deputy in the present, but a potential Mike Maignan successor down the line.

There will also be two crucial duels involving the two Nagys, Oliver and Adam. The former will play at right-back and faces the difficult task of keeping Alphadjo Cisse quiet. The Italian is the Rossoneri’s top scorer this season and will be champing at the bit to build on his hat-trick against RB Salzburg. Oliver Nagy is dangerous going forward though, with two assists in his five starts, so Cisse will have to help out defensively too.

Adam Nagy meanwhile faces the task of stopping Milan’s second-top scorer, Adrien Rabiot. The Frenchman netted his fifth of the season in the derby against Inter, and Amorim has chosen to rely on his experience against an opponent who is also 31 years of age. The Hungarian signed from Spezia in the summer and is best known for his appearances at the 2016, 2020 and 2024 UEFA European Championships for his national team.

Ferencvaros have two main threats that Milan must keep quiet, especially the way that this game could play out with the visitors no doubt keen to contain and counter. Bamidele Yusuf is the first, and the Nigerian is expected to start up front this evening though he can also play and drift wide. He has six goals and three assists in 10 starts this season for the green and whites.

Bamidele Yusuf 🎯#UEL | @Fradi_HU pic.twitter.com/AXnt4XPaSu

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) October 29, 2026

Sanhoun Diawara will have to do his bit to keep Yusuf quiet, but our feeling is that Koni De Winter will take on the man-marking duties just like he did with Inter’s lone striker Marcus Thuram in the derby. The Belgian has been undroppable in a literal sense, so we hope that no signs of fatigue are seen especially in transition, like against Bologna.

The visitors’ other danger man is Kristoffer Zachariassen, who matches Yusuf on nine goal contributions (seven goals, two assists) for the season. The 32-year-old Norwegian has plenty of experience and an eye for goal from the attacking midfield role, though his heat maps show he tends to drift to the right too.

So, it will be down to Ardon Jashari to keep tabs on him. Amorim and Milan are still waiting for the Swiss to put together a good run of solid starts after his arrival from Club Brugge for over €30m, and this is the kind of game that he needs to seize control of and dominate to show he is capable of being the anchor man, especially with Luka Modric’s retirement surely not far away.

#1930. Emery would be mad to go to United - his best route to the top is at Villa. They're close to being giants and, with him as boss, they can bridge the gap to the elite: OLIVER HOLT

Published: 04:22 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 06:11 EDT, 3 November 2026

Unai Emery, the man of the moment, the manager whose name is on everybody’s lips, the man that others would make their king, walked into the cavernous press conference room at the Nou Camp just after 8.15pm local time on Monday evening.

This is only a league game, early in the competition but there was electricity in the room that comes with the anticipation of the collision ahead. ‘This is elite football and Barcelona is always the favourite in a competition like this,’ Emery reminded his audience, ‘but we also have a history.

‘In 1982, we won the Champions League, the so-called European Cup. Barcelona are the favourites because of the present and what they have done over the last ten years. We are constantly seeking new challenges. We want to come here tomorrow night and see how far away we are from Barcelona.’

This is Emery against a big club. Against one of the modern elite. This is Emery and his wits against Lamine Yamal and Rodri and Raphinha. This is what Jamie Carragher, one of Emery’s most vocal – and controversial - champions of recent days, would call a ‘giant’ club. The phrase ‘Mes Que Un Club’ is even written into the seats at this magnificent stadium. It is the kind of club many believe Emery is born for.

Everybody is lavishing praise upon him. A few hours earlier, at the Barcelona training complex in Sant Joan Despi, several miles west of the city, Hansi Flick, the Barca coach, waxed lyrical about Emery’s talents and said he was the reason they were expecting such a tough match in their Champions League tie here on Tuesday evening.

‘Unai Emery is one of the best coaches in Europe and the world,’ Flick said. ‘He is very successful. In the way his team plays, you can see a clear structure in defence. And in offence, they have different patterns. For me, it is amazing to see his team.

At the Barcelona training complex, Hansi Flick, the Barca coach, waxed lyrical about Emery’s talents and said he was the reason they were expecting such a tough match

Flick also praised Nicolas Jackson, the Villa striker who has found his form under Emery

‘Their start this season was not easy, but they came back. You can see the confidence they have on the ball, how they play out, and Nicolas Jackson is at an unbelievable level. For us, it will be a tough game against a good team and, as well, a great coach.’

Anthony Gordon, who joined Barcelona from Newcastle United in the summer, had already given a press conference of impressive maturity and thoughtfulness that had taken in his love of books and his distrust of TikTok but he, too, was unstinting in his admiration for Emery.

'Villa are a very good team,’ Gordon said. ‘They have one of the best coaches in the world right now. They are on a great run of late as well, so it will be a difficult game. They are one of the teams who are always in a game and are always ready for any type of game. It will be a very tough challenge.’

Even the environs of the stadium seemed to pay homage to Emery’s talents. Cranes still lean over the stands here as the extensive renovations to the steepling stands continue. Emery, we all know, is the master of the rebuild.

So by the time Emery walked out into that auditorium, it felt almost as if this were a final audition. This is the kind of stuff that, understandably, enrages Villa and their fans because of its patronising tone but the more impressive his results with his club, the more people suggest he should go elsewhere.

That is what got Carragher in trouble. Carragher said Manchester United should be making him their number one target because he is the best manager in the league. ‘Surely, he would want the opportunity to manage a giant again,’ Carragher said, aiming a couple of expletives at Villa supporters for good measure.

Villa chairman Nassef Sawiris threatened to take legal action against Carragher, Carragher apologised and all was forgotten. But while Emery thrives and a manager at one of the elite European clubs struggles, he will continue to be linked to those positions. It is the way it has always been.

And anyway, Emery would be mad to go to United if Michael Carrick leaves Old Trafford in the next few weeks. Not just because United is a basket-case of a club run by people who would not allow the manager to have anything like the level of control he enjoys at Villa, where he has smart owners who trust him and support him to the hilt.

Emery has been talked about as a successor to Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Emery knows what it can be like at so-called bigger clubs like PSG and Arsenal, when impatience runs wild and expectations are absurd and support starts to wane. His best route to the very top is at a club like Villa. Because Villa are close to being giants and, with him as boss, they can bridge the gap to the elite.

Emery lost most of his first team in the summer - Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Lucas Digne, Emiliano Martinez, Youri Tielemans, Ollie Watkins, Donyell Malen and Leon Bailey all left – but he has fashioned a new exciting side in their stead already.

Villa are unbeaten in their last five games in the Premier League, including a victory that handed Manchester City their first defeat of the season, and sit second only to PSG at the top of the nascent Champions League table, with three straight wins. Emery is burnishing his reputation as a football magician. He is the game’s hottest managerial property again.

If Villa get a result at the Nou Camp, speculation about the future of Emery, who will turn 55 on the day of the game, will run wild again. It is bound to. It is a compliment to both manager and club, although it is unlikely Villa will see it that way. The joy of the results he is producing is tempered only by the fear of losing him.

But for all his success in Europe – he has won the Europa League five times, most recently with Villa in Istanbul last summer – he has a miserable record at the Nou Camp. He has brought six different clubs here and lost 14 of the 15 matches he has managed. His sole victory was with Villarreal in May 2022.

He has one particular ghost to slay in this competition. Because the Nou Camp was the scene of La Remontada, or ‘the comeback’, when Emery’s PSG brought a 4-0 lead to Barcelona for the second leg of a Round of 16 tie. PSG had won the first leg at the Parc des Princes 4-0 in March 2017 but Barcelona swept them aside 6-1 back in Catalonia.

The mention of that game was the one time during the press conference when Emery bristled. When asked what his memory of it was, he said sharply: ‘One more.’ Just one game among hundreds, he seemed to be saying. ‘I played in Europe 16 years in a row and I have learned in all of them. I learned so, so much. That night, I learned on sports side and not the sports side.’

Alongside him, John McGinn spoke compellingly, too. He spoke about coming here just once before, on a stadium tour when he was eight years old and he and his family were on their way to a holiday in the Canary Islands.

Emery has one particular ghost to slay in this competition because the Nou Camp was the scene of La Remontada, when his PSG side lost despite coming with a 4-0 lead in the first leg

‘I am 32 years old and the trajectory of this club is allowing me to dream the dream of playing in front of the biggest crowds in the biggest arenas,’ McGinn said. ‘We want to make this a yearly experience to compete with the biggest teams in England and Europe.’

Emery also mentioned Gordon as one of the components he admires in the Barcelona side. Listening to him earlier, it was clear that he has already grown, both on and off the pitch since his move to Spanish football.

‘The challenge of joining Barca is different to what I've had before,’ Gordon said, ‘because when I was at Everton, I was fighting relegation for two or three years, which was tough. At Newcastle we were fighting for the Champions League and to push up the tables, and now I am at a club where we are fighting for every trophy.

‘I really enjoyed all three because they come with different things to help you as a person, help you grow. I think to be competing on every front for every trophy is definitely the most enjoyable. I think people think it's more pressure, but it's actually less pressure than fighting relegation and fighting to push up the table for the Champions League. I want to win every trophy. I want to be the best. This club allows me to do so.’

Before he left, Gordon spoke about how he rations his time on social media and reads more books and goes on more walks. ‘When you're in that wheel of dopamine addiction and you're scrolling on social media, you have to come away from it and get back to what’s real,’ he said.

On Tuesday night in the Nou Camp, Emery and Villa will take the next step on their advance on Europe and the rest of us will find out what is real and what is not.

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 14:48, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 14:51

Real Betis will aim to make it successive wins in Spain's top flight when they continue their campaign against Elche at Estadio Martinez Valero on Sunday afternoon.

The Green-Striped Ones were beaten 1-0 by Valencia in their last match, but that proved to be their first loss in five games in all competitions.

Martin Anselmi's side have actually won two of their last three matches, including a 3-1 victory over Pinatar in the Copa del Rey at the end of October.

Elche have struggled in their recent meetings with Real Betis, losing four of the last five fixtures between the two sides, but the corresponding game last season finished 1-1.

Elche will be without the services of Marc Aguado and Thomas Lemar for this weekend's match through injury, but the home side are otherwise in strong form.

Yago Santiago and Gonzalo Villar had both been doubts for this contest, but the pair are available for selection, while Pedro Bigas should also again be in the squad.

Lemar's position in the starting side is likely to be taken by Facundo Buonanotte, while there will be a spot through the middle for Fer Nino, who has netted six times in La Liga this season.

As for Real Betis, Cucho Hernandez remains on the sidelines and is unlikely to be back in the fold for the Seville outfit until the end of November.

Facundo Bernal is still suspended, but Junior Firpo and Alvaro Fidalgo are both expected to be back in the squad after recent absences.

Troy Parrott has not scored for Real Betis since the start of September, but the 24-year-old is expected to continue through the middle for Pellegrini's team.

#1925. Asia Cup is POSTPONED just two months before its start due to safety concerns in Saudi Arabia - in huge boost to Premier League clubs

Published: 03:25 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 06:13 EDT, 3 November 2026

The 2027 Asia Cup has been delayed by almost a year amid the ongoing Middle East crisis.

Less than two months before it was due to kick off, the tournament hosted by Saudi Arabia has been postponed until December 2027 after the Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict re-escalated.

Major airports in Saudi Arabia are operating reduced services after a missile attack by Yemen's Houthi movement on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people. Two people were also killed after an attack at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

It makes the tournament not only a logistical nightmare for the 24 participating teams but also raises serious safety concerns.

A statement from the Asian Football Confederation said: 'The Organising Committee for AFC Asian Cup approved rescheduling the flagship national team tournament considering the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions.

'The new dates of the tournament (December 23 2027 to January 21 2028) will be presented to FIFA for approval.

'Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organisation and delivery of the Competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.'

However, the delay boosts several Premier League clubs, who no longer face losing players for up to a month of the season. Japan had ten Premier League players available for selection, with Aston Villa potentially losing first-choice goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

Aston Villa could have been without Zion Suzuki, who has kept three clean sheets this season, for five Premier League matches and their last two league phase matches in the Champions League

Japan international Daichi Kamada has started all nine of Crystal Palace's Premier League matches this season

Crystal Palace could have been without Takehiro Tomiyasu and Daichi Kamada for up to five Premier League matches had Japan reached the final.

Ipswich's Daizen Maeda, who has made ten appearances this season, was likely to be called up alongside Brighton's Kaoru Mitoma, who is currently sidelined.

Manchester City, meanwhile, were expected to lose Uzbek international Abdukodir Khusanov.

This is the second successive tournament to be postponed after the 2023 edition was delayed by a year due to the Covid pandemic.

The Asia Cup is not the first event in Saudi Arabia to be disrupted after the PIF-backed Asian Tour Saudi International golf tournament was indefinitely postponed.

Meanwhile, the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament - featuring Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev - in Riyadh has been cancelled.

It is not a complete whitewash, though. Last weekend, Canelo Alvarez reclaimed the WBC super-middleweight title, beating Christian Mbilli on points in Riyadh. Riyadh will also play host to WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday.

The Formula 1 season concludes in the Middle East, with the penultimate race taking place in Qatar at the end of the month, followed by the season finale in Abu Dhabi at the start of December.

F1 intends to go ahead with both races but is continuing to monitor the situation.

Meanwhile, the second race of next season is scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia in mid-March. There are currently no plans to cancel the event, despite this year's race having been called off.

#1924. St Johnstone boss banishes Dundee demons with ‘bitter’ declaration

Simo Valakari was thrilled to give St Johnstone supporters a 2-1 victory over Dundee to celebrate after recent Perth struggles against their Tayside rivals.

Dundee won twice at McDiarmid Park in 2024-25, the season Saints were relegated, but a transformed team has returned to the top flight under Valakari.

“We are a totally new team and it is not good to hold on to all those memories,” said Valakari. “Me as a manager, of course I remember. At Christmas-time we were 3-0 down after 20 minutes of the biggest game of the season.

“And of course I remember when their fans were on the pitch celebrating on the last day. But my players don’t have this baggage. We are creating new experiences together; this is our new adventure.

“If I carried everything that happened in the past with me, I would be a very bitter person! You need to let things go; that’s why we didn’t even bring it up.

“But all the players knew how much this game meant to our fans. We needed to perform, and we did. And to perform the way we did against a very good team made it a deserved win.”

Josh Campbell headed Saints in front after five minutes before substitute Joe Westley replied early in the second half following a mix-up between goalkeeper Ross Sinclair and Cheick Diabate. Kai Fotheringham, on his first Premiership start for Saints, netted a deflected winner in the 72nd minute.

“We were very good in the first half,” said Valakari. “They changed things at half-time. It took us a bit of time to adjust and we conceded a goal in that period.

“My team showed their character and personality again. We got control back and it got better and better from that.”

Dundee manager Steven Pressley conceded that his team failed to match much of their early-season form. He admitted St Johnstone were deserving winners over the course of the match.

“Over the course of the 90 minutes, St Johnstone were probably deserving of the victory,” he said. “We didn’t quite reach the heights and the standards that we’ve set.

“It’s not a criticism, it’s just these players continuously produced really high performances and have set some incredible standards. We were just a little bit below them on some of the things that we pride ourselves on.

“And, on the things we pride ourselves on, I thought St Johnstone were very strong. We’re disappointed to go into an international break on a defeat.”

#1920. Jude Bellingham's Dad scores SEVEN for England's OVER-50s side on same day superstar son nets for Real Madrid

Published: 06:17 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 06:18 EDT, 3 November 2026

Jude Bellingham's father Mark scored seven goals as he represented an England veterans side in a match against the Republic of Ireland.

Bellingham played up front for England Veterans' Over 50s side in a 13-1 victory on Sunday.

The 50-year-old struck six times in the first half of the match and provided an assist to give England a 7-0 lead at the break.

Bellingham added his seventh of the match in the second half as the England side cruised to victory.

Mark's goalscoring feat came on the same day that superstar son Jude scored in Real Madrid's 3-0 victory over Racing de Santander in LaLiga.

The Bellingham family were denied a unique hat-trick over the weekend, with Jobe having seen a goal ruled out as Borussia Dortmund were beaten 2-1 by Bayern Munich on Saturday.

Mark Bellingham, circled, scored seven goals for England Veterans' Over 50's team against the Republic of Ireland on Sunday. Source: Facebook/EVFC

The father of Real Madrid superstar Jude, 23, and Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe, Mark played for the England Veterans' Over 50's side for the first time (Source: judebellingham/Instagram)

The Bellingham family came close to a unique hat-trick at the weekend as Jude scored for Real Madrid, but Jobe had a goal disallowed as Borussia Dortmund lost to Bayern Munich

A talented non-league striker in his heyday, Mark Bellingham netted over 700 goals across at least 20 different clubs, including Leamington, Stourbridge and Sutton Coldfield Town.

He even earned the nickname the 'Non-League Pele' during his 25-year career, which ended in 2017.

Mark made his first appearance for England Veterans Over 50s side, who were crowned Seniors World Cup champions this year, clinching their ninth title in Thailand.

When not playing football of his own, Bellingham is regularly seen attending his two sons' matches.

A Southend United supporter, Mark introduced Jude to football, with the England star's first live matches coming alongside his father at Roots Hall.

Speaking about his father in a recent interview, Jude said: 'We talk about footballing heroes, and my dad was like my first.

'When you go and watch him play every week in non-league, you know it's not the Premier League or anything, but seeing the way that he played and the atmosphere, it made me fall in love with football so he was probably my first hero.

'After the first few times of going, I'd start to pay a bit more attention to the games and stuff, the atmosphere and he's scoring goals so you see him celebrating and stuff like that - you want that to be me.

'Growing up, he'd always give me tips on what I could do and now it gets to a certain age and it sort of flips and that's brilliant because we have that sort of relationship like father and son and then as I got older, like coach and player.'

Mark helped set up Stourbridge Juniors, Jude’s first club, and was a sergeant before fully focusing on his sons’ careers.

He became their agent and negotiated Jude’s £88.5million transfer to Real Madrid from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, and dealt with Dortmund again when Jobe moved there from Sunderland in 2025.

A former West Midlands Police officer, Bellingham earned the nickname the 'Non-League Pele' during his 25-year career. Pictured above with Jude (Source: CJPhillips1982/X)

Mark and Jude and Jobe's mother, Denise, are understood to have separated but remain close, the pair having attended Jude's games at the World Cup together this past summer

While in Germany, Mark reportedly held an emotional discussion with Dortmund sporting director Sebastian Kehl after being left unhappy by Jobe's substitution at half-time during his Bundesliga debut.

German publication BILD added at the time that Mark sought a meeting with manager Niko Kovac directly – and 'made no secret of his opinion'. The club proceeded to ban all family members from the dressing room following the incident.

Mark’s influence as an agent is said to have stretched to Jude’s media duties when with England. Notably, the player has gone out of his way to speak more at this most recent World Cup, but at previous tournaments he had avoided speaking beyond his obligations despite his increasing influence within the squad.

Mark and Jude and Jobe's mother, Denise, are understood to have separated but remain close, the pair having attended Jude's games at the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico this past summer.

#1916. West Ham star's WAG aims brutal parting dig at Nuno Espirito Santo after Hammers sacked under-fire manager - while team-mate 'likes' club post confirming his exit

Published: 03:40 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 06:25 EDT, 3 November 2026

Nuno Espirito Santo has been sacked by West Ham after a difficult start to the season, with Scott Parker poised to take over.

The Championship promotion favourites are eighth, so far struggling to live up to their billing after being relegated from the Premier League last season.

The former Tottenham, Wolves and Nottingham Forest manager, 52, signed a three-year contract in September 2025 but failed to stop the Hammers from crashing out of the top flight after a poor start to the season.

They were expected to start strongly in the second tier, yet Saturday's 3-1 home defeat by West Bromwich Albion left them with just six wins in 13 matches before Nuno's fate was confirmed on Tuesday morning.

Shortly after that news was confirmed, Marrion Areola, wife of West Ham's back-up keeper Alphonse, aimed a brutal parting dig at Nuno on her Instagram account.

Marrion, who had previously attacked Nuno after last season's relegation for dropping her husband, shared a series of Instagram stories where she appeared to express her joy at the news.

Nuno Espirito Santo has been sacked by West Ham with the club eighth in the Championship

Marrion Areola, wife of West Ham keeper Alphonse, aimed a brutal parting shot at Nuno

In one, she was smiling and posing for a photo, while in another she was skipping through the streets with Sam Phillips' 'Happy' song playing in the background.

In a third story, she shared a video from the famous film Sound of Music of So Long Farewell being sung.

Within the song, which is performed by the seven von Trapp children, a series of lyrics including 'so long', 'farewell', 'good night', 'Auf Wiedersehen', 'Adieu' and 'Au revoir' are mentioned in what is believed to her parting shot at Nuno.

West Ham's Instagram post announcing Nuno's exit, meanwhile, was liked by out of favour Mexican midfielder Edson Alvarez, who is yet to feature in the Championship this season.

George Earthy, a former academy graduate who now plays for Reading, also appeared to like the post.

Back in the summer, Marrion had taken to social media to target Nuno and former boss Graham Potter in a series of posts, blaming the pair for West Ham's relegation and hitting out at the pair for dropping her husband.

Marrion initially shared an image of Areola holding up the Conference League trophy in 2023 and stated: 'From a trophy to relegation. Thank you Potter for the start of this season and Nuno for the end.'

In another, Marrion accused Nuno of dropping her husband - who lost his place to Mads Hermansen - 'for no particular reason'.

'Being dropped at the beginning of the season for no reason,' Marrion wrote. 'Being back after a very bad start and then has made 20 games and all of a sudden: "I'm really sorry - you won't start", "Why?", "For no particular reason but I'm sorry".'

Marrion also shared a post from December that stated Areola had the highest save percentage in the Premier League, before adding on the club's relegation: 'Very sad day for the fans. Very frustrated for the family. But always proud of you no matter what.'

She then placed the blame on Nuno for Areola missing out on France's squad for the World Cup.

Sharing highlights from Areola's five appearances for France's national team she wrote: 'And NO World Cup this year, thank you Nuno'.

Meanwhile, it is understood that Parker is set to replace the Portuguese boss, with the former West Ham midfielder having been out of work since leaving Burnley shortly after their relegation from the Premier League was confirmed last season.

Parker, who has won promotion to the top flight as a manager with Fulham, Bournemouth and the Clarets, made 129 appearances for the Hammers between 2007 and 2012, winning three Player of the Year awards during his time at the club.

Former West Ham midfielder Scott Parker is poised to replace Nuno at the London Stadium

Nuno's dismissal comes after the Hammers were beaten 3-1 by West Brom on Saturday

In a club statement on Tuesday morning, West Ham had said: 'West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espirito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

'Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

'Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

'West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

'The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway.'

The club added that Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville would take temporary charge of the team ahead of Wednesday's trip to Cardiff City.

However, it is believed that Parker will be in charge for that game if a deal is agreed in time, and that Noble, a former team-mate of his, could be part of his backroom team.

Many had expected Nuno to depart in the aftermath of relegation – and Daily Mail Sport understands that Hammers co-owner David Sullivan wanted to part ways with the Portuguese coach – but Daniel Kretinsky, now the club's largest shareholder, backed him to lead the club's promotion charge.

After that decision, the club released a statement outlining their plans and revealed that Nuno was 'highly motivated' for the challenge ahead.

Despite the high-profile sales of Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville in the summer, West Ham kept the likes of Jarrod Bowen, Tomas Soucek, Taty Castellanos and Konstantinos Mavropanos.

They also invested heavily in the squad, which included the addition of Arne Engels from Celtic for a Championship record fee of £22million.

Although they picked up 6-0 victories over Wrexham and Lincoln City, Nuno's side struggled for consistency, and back-to-back defeats by Southampton and West Brom in recent weeks proved to be the final straw.

During and after the defeat by the Baggies, home fans at the London Stadium turned on Nuno and subjected him to chants of 'sacked in the morning'.

Speaking to the media afterwards, Nuno outlined his desire to turn things around.

'Every day there is pressure,' he said. 'I’m disappointed because we wanted to improve things. We want to win matches.

'This (the chants) is the reality. You can only change this if we win games. That’s the solution: getting better results. We have to go back to good performances.

'We dropped points against Burnley (in the season opener), we lost (at home) to Charlton, Southampton and West Brom. The only solution is to improve our game. When we do that, our fans are going to stick with us. They’re going to support us.'

West Ham co-owner David Sullivan had wanted to part ways with Nuno back in the summer

West Ham have suffered back-to-back defeats after last season's Premier League relegation

There is a certain irony to the defeat by West Brom being the end for Nuno given he is a legendary former manager of their arch-rivals Wolves.

But, despite an upturn in form at the back-end of last season and an eight-game unbeaten run earlier in this campaign, he departs the London Stadium with a record of 19 wins, 19 defeats and 15 draws from 53 matches in charge.

After the Cardiff game, West Ham – who are six points adrift of table-toppers Middlesbrough – face a trip to Blackburn before the two-week international break.

#1915. Jim Goodwin bites tongue with ‘careful’ admission after VAR intervention

Boss Jim Goodwin hit out at the decision to award the penalty that cost Dundee United dear in a 1-1 draw against Motherwell at Tannadice.

Referee Ryan Lee had initially given a free-kick for offside in the early stages of the game.

However, he was then advised by VAR Andrew Dallas to have another look at an incident where Tawanda Maswanhise had gone down in the United box under a challenge by home skipper Dylan Tait.

After checking the pitchside monitor, the whistler pointed to the spot with Motherwell captain Lukas Fadinger tucking the penalty away.

The Terrors ultimately salvaged a point thanks to a Jesse Randall goal but Goodwin insisted his side should have had all three.

He said: “It’s a poor decision for me. I know it’s going to be subjective and people will have their own opinions on it, but I don’t know what Dylan Tait is meant to do.

“We all know Maswanhise runs at pace, he’s driving at the defender and I think he’s going down before the contact arrives.

“Dylan is pulling out and I just don’t understand what a defender is meant to do in that situation.

“The linesman initially was giving an offside but neither he or the ref thought there was a foul in that particular instance.

“We were happy with that but when VAR check it there’s not the offside and they decide to carry on the check into the penalty incident.

“I need to be careful what I say because I got in trouble a few years ago talking about players going over easily in the penalty area.

“But I think a bit of experience, knowing the type of players you’re dealing with, the referee at that moment made the right call.

“When the referee got called to the monitor, you have an experienced referee there basically telling a young ref he’s made a mistake.

“So it takes a bit of courage for the ref on the park to overrule that decision from the VAR room. It’s gone against us but we reacted positively.”

Not surprisingly, Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson disagreed with Goodwin’s assessment of the penalty decision and instead insisted it should have been awarded.

The 36-year-old said: “I haven’t watched it back with a close-up on the situation in the box yet but the way I saw it JT (Maswanhise) is running at high speed into the box. He’s on the ball and gets down from a tackle, and it’s a penalty.

“So it depends on who you ask. None of us can complain with the draw, it was a very tight game. It was very open but definitely fair with the draw.”

#1914. Celtic vs Kilmarnock - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 06 Nov 2026 15:05, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 20:38

Looking to move seven points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership, Celtic return to league action on Sunday when they welcome Kilmarnock to Glasgow for their second meeting this season.

The Bhoys secured a dramatic second-half comeback victory over Besiktas in the Europa League during the week, while Killie head into this encounter on the back of a 2-2 draw with St Johnstone on Halloween.

After drawing with Dundee United and suffering their first defeat to Falkirk in nearly two decades, Martin O'Neill and his Celtic side went into their midweek clash with Turkish giants Besiktas in desperate need of a positive result, having dropped to second-bottom in the Europa League league-phase table.

The Bhoys produced a lacklustre first-half display at Celtic Park on Thursday night, managing just two touches in the opposition box during the opening 45 minutes. When they fell 1-0 behind shortly after the restart, it looked as though the Glasgow giants were heading for another disappointing European result.

However, substitutes Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran inspired a remarkable turnaround as Celtic took the lead, were pegged back in the 85th minute and then responded once again to secure a 3-2 victory over Vincenzo Italiano's side.

The three points provided a much-needed boost for O'Neill's men, whose lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership had been cut after collecting just one point from their previous two league outings.

Despite the demanding nature of their European comeback, the result could provide the confidence needed to spark an improvement in domestic performances.

Celtic currently hold a four-point advantage at the summit, although arch-rivals Rangers have a game in hand and could move above them if the Bhoys fail to return to winning ways on Sunday.

As for Kilmarnock, they travel to Glasgow seeking their first victory over Celtic since December 2023, having failed to win any of their previous 10 meetings with the Scottish champions.

Having finished third-bottom last season, Kilmarnock avoided the relegation playoffs with four consecutive victories to close out the 2025-26 campaign, but they would have been hoping to build on that strong finish rather than find themselves battling near the foot of the table again.

Under Neil McCann, who has won 36% of his matches since taking charge in January 2026, Kilmarnock have struggled for consistency and currently sit 11th in the 12-team division.

Two wins, three draws and seven defeats from their opening 12 matches have left McCann's side with just nine points, highlighting several areas that need to improve sooner rather than later.

Defensive frailties have been a particular concern, with Killie already conceding 28 goals at an average of 2.3 per game.

That is comfortably the worst defensive record in the Scottish Premiership, with second-highest Motherwell and St Mirren having shipped 20.

Celtic emerged from their European victory without any further injury concerns, although changes are likely after Duran and Osmand made an impact from the bench, with the former scoring twice and the latter also finding the net.

James Forrest and Sebastian Tounekti could be the players to make way, allowing both substitutes to earn starting roles.

Canadian full-back Alistair Johnston and Yang Hyun-Jun remain sidelined through injury, although both are expected to return in the coming weeks.

As for the visitors, McCann could stick with the same starting XI that drew 2-2 with 10-man St Johnstone as he looks to find some much-needed consistency.

Former Manchester United academy product Joe Hugill is expected to retain his place up front as he looks to build on the four goal involvements he has recorded this season.

McCann will be without Bailey Rice and Maksymillian Stryjek.

Johnstone; Lotomba, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; Nygren, McGregor, Baur; Duran, Hogh, Osmand

Manti; McCarthy, Deas, Stanger; Brandon, Tshibola, Lowery, Ring; Kiltie; Hugill, Daniels

Although Celtic have been inconsistent in recent weeks, their comeback victory over Besiktas should provide a timely confidence boost, and we expect them to return to winning ways in the league on Sunday.

Kilmarnock have looked particularly vulnerable defensively this season, and we believe the hosts will have enough attacking quality to exploit those weaknesses and secure a comfortable 3-0 victory.

Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing.

➤ The Diavolo suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures.

➤ Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967-68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level.

➤ Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

#1912. Kasper Hogh riddle continues to fox Celtic as Martin O'Neill opens up on misfiring striker

“Kasper had a brilliant game. That's the life of a striker - you have to be there to take them. His all-round game today was very good. He gave us a platform to play.”

Sunday, August 9, the words of Celtic assistant coach Shaun Maloney after watching striker Kasper Hogh score a 33-minute hat-trick in a 5-1 win over Kilmarnock.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hogh had not long arrived at Celtic from Bodo/Glimt for £12 million, a record signing for the Scottish champions. His predatory instincts in Ayrshire led many to believe the Dane was on his way to the golden boot.

Fifteen games on for Celtic, Hogh has not scored a goal since. In fact, his manager Martin O’Neill is yet to see him find the net, as he was recovering from a “small procedure” for the match at Rugby Park.

Maybe the visit of Kilmarnock, who he terrorised on that summer’s afternoon, on Sunday will be the match where Hogh finally finds the net again. That is, of course, if the 25-year-old gets the nod in attack.

Hogh’s star is waning. The 25-year-old has been eclipsed by fellow July signing Camilo Duran, who has netted 13 times this season and clambered off the bench to help Celtic defeat Besiktas on Thursday night. The Colombian did more in his half-hour cameo than Hogh did in double that time. The poor hitman didn’t touch the ball once in the Turkish penalty box in the opening period.

It would be unfair to judge Hogh wholly on his goals, although at £4m per strike so far, that is an expensive outlay. Physical and hard-working, he offers Celtic a focal point. O’Neill was pleased with his performance against Besiktas. “I want centre-forwards to be able to hold it and that is what he did,” said the manager. “He is not Duran, he is not a dribbler. But if he can do this for us against strong opposition it will stand him in good stead.”

Hogh’s belief is bound to be low. How could it not be? He is out of the Denmark squad for the first time in over a year and when he tapped in from an already rescinded free-kick against Besiktas, there was a slightly sarcastic cheer from the home crowd. The misfiring forward is a real talking point.

“I think Thursday night will be good for him,” continued O’Neill. “I said to him that I’m not worried about whether he scores a goal. Of course you want centre-forwards to score and of course centre-forwards live on them. But I said to him that last night I wanted him to be strong and fight when the ball is played up to him. I thought in terms of holding the ball up and bringing people into the game that he did really well.

“Centre-forwards need a goal. But that performance there against European opposition will give him confidence. I don’t know what side we will play him on Sunday. But this lad has scored goals in the Champions League, remember. He will get a confidence boost from last night in terms of doing that part of the game well. But it will be nice for him to score a goal.”

The problem Hogh perhaps had is that O’Neill will turn to Duran more often than not now. “At this minute, he is on fire,” added O’Neill of the South American. “He can play wide right, he has done that. He has played wide left. But centre forward is where he is dynamic.” For now, unlike his strike partner.

#1908. Nicky Butt doubles down on Michael Carrick's 'management's not for me' claim - as he pinpoints moment under-fire Man United boss made comment

Published: 07:20 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 07:21 EDT, 3 November 2026

Former Manchester United star Nicky Butt has doubled down on his bizarre claim that Michael Carrick told him 'management's not for me' before he took the job at Old Trafford.

Carrick, 45, returned to the club where he earned legendary status as a player in January in the aftermath of Ruben Amorim's sacking.

Despite a strong end to last season when he guided United to third place, Carrick is under huge pressure this time around after picking up just seven points from nine matches.

Speaking last month, Butt revealed that Carrick had told him he would only return to management for the United job after his sacking by Middlesbrough in June 2025, a claim the current Red Devils boss subsequently laughed off.

Yet, Butt, appearing on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan, has reaffirmed his stance and pinpointed the exact moment when Carrick told him he didn't want to get back in the dugout.

'I believe I said that but I’ll clarify what I meant,' Butt said. 'And I’m not ducking it, I’m really not, I’ll explain. I was playing in a padel tournament with Michael, he’s my doubles partner, and I was talking about football and Middlesbrough.

Former Manchester United star Nicky Butt has doubled down on his bizarre claim that Michael Carrick told him 'management's not for me' before he took the job at Old Trafford

Speaking on Football Uncensored, Butt revealed the exact moment that Carrick made the claim

'I had a beer after it, and I was like "so what’s your plans mate? What do you think you’re going to do when you get back into management?"

'He said "no, it’s all over the show, it’s hard work – however, if the big one came up, obviously I would take it".'

Butt continued: 'And the big one did come up, and he took it, and that wasn’t a case of me saying Michael didn’t want the Man United job, it was a case of he didn’t want a job.

'He didn’t want to go driving up and down the M6 all day when he’s got kids at home for no reward.

'But if the big one comes, which I assume was Man United, then he’d take it. That’s the facts of the conversation that I had with him.'

When pressed on Butt's comments ahead of United's draw with Leeds last month, Carrick had said: 'I definitely wouldn't be here if that was the case, would I? At this stage, it's the best job and the best role I could possibly have.

'I feel a real privilege of being in this position and a real responsibility, but equally a drive of wanting to make a difference and having success here.

'I'm loving it. I love the situation when actually you get some sort of struggle and you've got to find a way out of it. I actually enjoy that because that's part of what drives you to have success.

'If you're not ready for that and you can't do anything that's difficult, then you're never going to be great. So we've got to work our way through it, and I'm enjoying it as we go.'

Butt claimed Carrick said he'd only return to management for 'the big job' at Man United

Butt's original claim had come on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast when he said: 'I was with Michael before he got the Man United job and spoke to him about management.

'He went "no it's not for me, it's too much, my head's all over the show, I'd only do it for the big job. The big job is Man United".

'So because that club's gone to him he's naturally going to go and do it. I think when he's gone through that door, put aside last year because like Scholesy said that's totally different to this year, I think he's realised he's gone into a club that's different to the club that he knew and was at.

'But these lads won't turn down Man United. Ole Gunnar (Solskjaer) wouldn't turn it down.

'Roy Keane might never turn that down. When that club comes calling and you've been at that football club, you don't turn it down.'

United and Carrick face a crunch week, with home games against Roma and Aston Villa coming ahead of next week's international break.

#1907. Liverpool's £123m Bradley Barcola problem: Iraola under scrutiny

By Naim Beneddra | 06 Nov 2026 15:17

Bradley Barcola's difficult start at Liverpool has raised questions about whether Andoni Iraola is making the best use of the French winger, with the manager himself acknowledging a significant difference in the player's performances depending on his position.

The 24-year-old arrived from Paris Saint-Germain in August in a deal worth up to £123m, but has struggled to reproduce the consistency that made him one of Europe's most exciting attacking talents.

His three Liverpool goals have all come in the same Champions League match against LASK, while he has contributed two assists in the Premier League. Thirteen appearances into his Anfield career, the return remains modest given the expectations surrounding his arrival.

However, Barcola's struggles cannot be explained by his finishing alone. He has featured in several attacking roles under Iraola, including an unfamiliar central position during Wednesday's 3-2 Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce.

The Spanish coach's subsequent assessment has brought a wider tactical question into focus: why has Liverpool's expensive summer signing spent so much time away from the position in which he is most effective?

Iraola's decision to deploy Barcola as a central striker in Istanbul was partly influenced by the availability of his other attacking players.

With Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz starting on the wings, Alexander Isak was initially kept on the bench, having been earmarked for a shorter appearance.

Liverpool's manager believed Barcola's acceleration could cause problems for Fenerbahce's defenders, particularly when attacking the space behind their back line.

"We thought it would work well because I think Bradley, in terms of speed and the match-ups, it could be good for him," Iraola explained after the defeat.

However, he acknowledged that the experiment had not produced the same attacking threat as some of Liverpool's more familiar combinations.

"All season he has been better when he has played outside wide," Iraola admitted.

The assessment was revealing, particularly given Barcola's preference for operating on the left.

Of his 13 Liverpool appearances, six have come away from that preferred position, including five on the right and Wednesday's experiment through the middle.

Barcola's greatest strengths are his acceleration, close control and ability to isolate defenders in one-on-one situations. On the left, he can receive the ball facing an opponent, accelerate into space and create opportunities with either a cutback or a direct run towards goal.

Operating centrally presents a different challenge.

Against teams defending with limited space between their centre-backs, he is required to receive more frequently with his back to goal, hold off defenders and make decisions in congested areas.

Those demands do not necessarily suit a player whose most dangerous actions often begin with a run from a wider position.

Iraola has not ruled out using him through the middle again, insisting that such an arrangement could be useful against particular opponents.

Nevertheless, Liverpool's attacking performance in Istanbul offered little evidence that it should become his regular role.

Isak scored after replacing Ngumoha in the second half, while the Reds were more threatening once they had greater presence in central areas.

Barcola has also been guilty of individual errors that cannot be attributed to his positioning.

Against Brentford, for example, he attempted an unsuccessful chip when through on goal and later lost possession after delaying a pass during a promising counter-attack.

His decision-making and finishing therefore remain legitimate areas for improvement, regardless of where Iraola selects him.

There are mitigating circumstances surrounding Barcola's arrival that help explain his uneven performances.

Liverpool agreed to pay PSG an initial £106m, with a further £17m in potential add-ons, making the Frenchman one of the most expensive signings in the club's history.

Yet the transfer was completed only towards the end of August, depriving him of a full pre-season with Iraola and his new teammates.

Barcola had also been involved in the World Cup during the summer, leaving him with limited preparation before adapting to a different league and a new tactical environment.

His first Liverpool appearance came in early September, following several weeks without competitive football.

The physical demands of the Premier League have presented another adjustment, while Liverpool's difficulties against compact defensive teams have not always allowed Barcola to exploit the space that made him so effective at PSG.

There is also the challenge of developing an understanding with teammates who are themselves adapting to Iraola's methods.

In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, published before the Fenerbahce defeat, Barcola acknowledged that he had yet to reach his best level.

"No, I don't think I'm at my best yet," he admitted. "You still haven't seen the best version of me."

The Frenchman believes improving his relationship with those around him will be crucial.

"On top of that, we're working with my team-mates so that they can make the most of my strengths," he explained.

"So yes, I think once we really develop that understanding, things will get much better."

Barcola's comments suggest that he recognises the need to improve without regarding his difficult start as evidence that the transfer has failed.

Nor does he consider his fee or the responsibility of succeeding Mohamed Salah to be an additional burden, insisting that he wants to establish his own identity at Anfield.

The challenge for Iraola is to find an attacking structure that helps him do so.

Ngumoha and Munoz have provided encouraging alternatives on the flanks, while Isak and Cody Gakpo offer different qualities through the middle. Those options give the Liverpool manager flexibility, but also complicate the task of establishing a settled role for Barcola.

The Reds travel to Crystal Palace on Sunday, when Iraola will have another opportunity to reconsider his attacking selection following the defeat in Turkey.

Barcola must improve his finishing and decision-making if he is to justify Liverpool's investment. But with his manager openly acknowledging that he performs better out wide, how consistently he is allowed to operate in that position will be an important part of assessing his progress.

#1906. GdS: A combined salary less than Ramos’ – the story behind the Ferencvaros ‘miracle’

AC Milan’s opponents Ferencvaros are one of a few teams to have a perfect record in the Europa League, and their story is a fascinating one.

Ferencváros arrive at San Siro having won all three of their league phase games thus far. In addition to that, they are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and they will go top of their domestic league if they win their game in hand. La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) share some insight on the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gonçalo Ramos’s gross salary €12.8m (€7m net including bonuses) is equivalent to the entire wage bill of Ferencváros. The combined salaries of the Hungarian club’s players total €11m.

Their highest earner is Naby Keïta, who accepted a contract worth just over €1.2m gross per season, seeking a career resurgence at the club with the largest payroll in the Hungarian league.

The Serbian midfielder Birmančević – formerly of Sparta Prague and Getafe, who arrived last summer – earns a slightly lower salary. Meanwhile, attacking midfielder Zachariassen earns around €700k and has scored three goals so far, as has Alphadjo Cissé.

In terms of wages, therefore, there is simply no comparison between the Rossoneri and Ferencváros. Yet, the Hungarians have won every match, while Milan have only three points. All the more reason not to take them lightly.

Gabor Kubatov has been on the board of Ferencváros since 2010, becoming president a year later. Under his leadership, the club has won eight Hungarian league titles. His personal history is quite unique: as a young man, he was a regular in ‘Sector 2’ – the section occupied by the ultras.

He later changed paths, and in 2006, he became a member of parliament, representing Fidesz, the party of Viktor Orbán. Despite his own background in the stands, his relationship with the Ferencváros ultras has not always been smooth.

In 2014, in an effort to combat violence and incidents of racism, Kubatov introduced a biometric identification system for stadium entry. A segment of the most ardent supporters responded by boycotting home matches, a protest that lasted for over three years.

An agreement was finally reached and the fans returned to the stands. With their support, Ferencváros went on to win seven consecutive league titles.

On 10 December 2017, a young Adam Nagy faced Milan while playing for Bologna. It didn’t go well: a 2-1 victory for the Rossoneri. Today, Nagy returns as a far more mature leader of his ‘miracle’ Ferencváros side.

Indeed, a significant portion of the Hungarian midfielder’s career has unfolded in Italy. He spent three years with the Rossoblù from 2016 to 2019 – following his initial breakthrough at Ferencváros – before returning to Italy in 2021 to join Pisa, having previously left to try his hand at Bristol City in England.

His most recent stint was with Spezia, which he departed this summer to return to his homeland. Yesterday, in a press conference, Rúben Amorim spoke very highly of him: “He is very skilled in the initial phase of build-up play.”

His ability to circulate the ball deep in his own half is his greatest strength. Conversely, he rarely ventures into the final third. The proof? Throughout all his years in Italy, he scored only one goal: against Verona in Serie A.

From the European champions Liverpool to Ferencvaros. Naby Keita – who will start on the bench tonight, hasn’t had the career he hoped for. Liverpool paid €65m to sign him from RB Leipzig in 2018, he won six more trophies in addition to the Champions League with Klopp’s English side.

In 2023, the Guinean midfielder moved to Werder Bremen, where he was left out of the squad after refusing to travel for the trip to Leverkusen because he wouldn’t have been a starter. Since January 2025, he has been at Ferencváros, who acquired him a year later.

Wearing a Liverpool shirt, Keïta has already beaten Milan at San Siro on 7 December 2021, a defeat that contributed to the Diavolo being eliminated in the group stage.

A less pleasant memory for Keïta involves his encounter with Luka Modrić when he came on in the final minutes of the 2022 Champions League final, which Liverpool lost to Real Madrid.

#1905. Rangers' Iron man of Ibrox always turned up - and should always be remembered

When Rangers TV released a short film about Harold Davis, the former Rangers player and war hero, on YouTube at the end of last month, the idea was to allow an important tribute to reach a wider audience.

It’s hard to imagine they could have predicted the initial interest. The mini documentary from RTV Studios has already attracted over 10,000 views. It is well on the way to the 100,000 (and counting) audience for a similarly essential homage to Davie Cooper to mark last year’s 30th anniversary of the wondrously talented winger’s dreadfully premature death.

Familiarise yourself with a tale of derring-do that ought to be turned into a blockbuster. It contains all the ingredients. Davis was in the process of establishing himself as a footballer with East Fife before National Service took him to Fort George, the Black Watch’s regimental base near Inverness, and then to the ‘forgotten war’ in Korea.

According to a telegram delivered to his parents’ house in Perth, “Corporal Harold Davis” was placed on the “dangerously ill” list after being gunned down at the Hook – a ridge around which much of the intense fighting took place – in May 1953.

As well as multiple stomach wounds, he sustained a shattered heel bone. A return to football seemed out of the question but after more than two years of rehabilitation, Scott Symon, his old East Fife manager, signed Davis for Rangers.

His incredible story certainly deserves a wider audience. I have to declare an interest because it’s now 20 years, almost to the day, since my then sports editor handed me an assignment that still ranks among the most memorable of my time in journalism. I was tasked with interviewing Davis for this newspaper.

Like so many things worth doing, it wasn’t a straightforward mission. We had to track Harold down first. Last heard of running a hotel in Gairloch, he had since moved with his wife Vi to Badachro, a small fishing village outside the Wester Ross town.

I drew up outside his beautiful home and sat rapt for hours in his company. When I made moves to leave – after all, a near five-hour drive back to Edinburgh loomed – I was instructed to stay the night. I did what I was told. Nobody disobeyed Harold – or Vi for that matter.

Another place was set at the dinner table and then we sat and watched the League Cup quarter-final between Hibs and Hearts while awaiting updates from Ibrox as Paul Le Guen’s Rangers hosted St Johnstone. A 2-0 home defeat underlined where the Ibrox side were at the time and prompted evident grumbles of disgust from the direction of Harold's chair.

The piece, when it appeared, was headlined: “The forgotten hero of a forgotten war". Harold isn’t forgotten now but it did seem like he was forgotten then. Not, I accept, by knowledgeable Rangers fans of a certain age, who recognised his distinction in bridging two eras.

When the right-half joined Rangers in 1956 he played with George Young, Ian McColl, Alex Scott and Johnny Hubbard. When he finished eight years later the likes of John Greig, Jim Baxter and Willie Henderson were in the team with him. He bridged two great eras and won four league championship medals, two League Cups and a Scottish Cup.

The medals are back on display at Ibrox. “Harold’s son Alan sold the medals to raise money for a local kids’ charity in the Gairloch area which unfortunately meant they were leaving Ibrox where they had been on display in the museum,” reports Tom Clark, a friend.

“But the wonderful news is that the buyer who bought them did not want the Rangers fans to miss out on seeing them and loaned them back to Rangers. They are now back in the exact same position where they were. So you have the double bonus of the medals being back on display and children benefitting in Harold’s name.”

Davis was a modest man but there was one claim he made on behalf of himself that sticks in my mind and remains true to this day.

“I might not have been the best player who ever put on a blue jersey,” he told me as the low winter sun dipped into Gairloch Bay. “But not one person who has put on a blue jersey started below where I had been in a physical sense and managed to reach the heights I did.”

It’s why he was so affronted by Jim Baxter’s casual attitude and tendency to turn up for games with the smell of the booze from the previous night – or from earlier the same day – still on his breath. He never toned down his disdain for his talented but wayward old teammate, whom he once pinned against an Ibrox dressing-room wall for some on-field insolence.

Rangers had no finer ambassador than Davis, who was delighted to be offered the honorary life president position of the Rangers Supporters Erskine Appeal (RSEA). This charity, founded by Clark to support Erskine homes for ex-service men and women, celebrates its 20th anniversary early next year and has raised £1.7 million to date.

It goes from strength to strength and remains inspired by Davis, who died eight years ago at the age of 85.

A chair is left empty at fund-raising dinners for both him and Vi, who passed away in 2023. It’s a deserved and poignant gesture but one that might cause Harold to smile. Being 'empty-chaired’ is a horrible modern term denoting those who haven’t contributed or haven’t turned up.

The Iron man of Ibrox always, always turned up. His contribution, while immense to Rangers, extended far beyond the club and merits the gratitude of all.

#1903. Celtic star's telepathic connection with strike partner and why his best is yet to come

Callum Osmand continues to highlight his considerable potential by making his mark at Celtic, but the young forward is adamant that what supporters have witnessed so far is only the beginning.

The 20-year-old has experienced a whirlwind introduction to first-team football in Glasgow, with the demands of competing for a place at one of Scotland's biggest clubs providing a steep learning curve. Yet his decisive contribution to Celtic's dramatic 3-2 Europa League victory over Besiktas offered another glimpse of the qualities that have made him such an intriguing prospect.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Introduced by Martin O’Neill in the second half, Osmand wasted little time making his presence felt against the Turkish side, scoring just 43 seconds after coming on before delivering a perfectly weighted pass for Camilo Duran to complete his double. His impact transformed the contest and secured Celtic a much-needed victory.

“Yeah, it was crazy. It's a surreal feeling when it's my first touch as well,” he reflected. “I was a bit nervous that I'd shanked it, but no, I'm happy that I caught it nicely. He (O’Neill) knows that I know what he expects from me, so it was about making sure I can come and bring some energy.”

His burgeoning partnership with Duran was another highlight. Their understanding was evident in the build-up to Celtic's vital third goal, with the former Fulham forward displaying excellent vision to pick out the Colombian's run in behind.

“I thought he was offside, to be honest!” Osmand admitted. “I was looking at the bench saying 'Close?', and they were like, 'Yeah, it's tight', but I know where he's going. He's such a sharp striker, so I know if I put that in the space, the keeper is not getting anywhere near it. He's a top, top player, so I can't fault him at all.”

Their connection is extending beyond the pitch, too. Despite a language barrier, Osmand feels the pair have struck up a genuine friendship.

“His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot,” he laughed. “I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now. Although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking. We talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but we get on really well.

“Camilo is unbelievable, a really top player. You can see even by the way he walks and the way he moves. I learn off him every day. He's a great guy.”

The victory over Besiktas could prove pivotal to Celtic's European ambitions, and Osmand hopes it will provide the confidence required to approach the remaining fixtures with greater freedom.

“For us, it felt like a must-win. That was our mindset going into the game and it’s a huge result,” he explained. “We knew we could still qualify, but we knew we had to get something out of Thursday night, and I think the boys done amazing.

“Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play, but as you can see, when we're confident, it just goes forward every time. We know when we're not playing as well, and we'll be the first, as players, to critique each other and critique ourselves before anyone else. It is about just staying together, building and getting a result like this to take into the next game.”

Osmand is equally candid about his own development, insisting there is still plenty of room for improvement despite his encouraging start. He pointed out what will be key to taking his game to the next level.

“I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally, and there's stuff I need to tidy up on, like decision-making and all this stuff,” Osmand admitted. “But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn. So on a personal note, that's what I want to do, just keep learning and keep understanding my role and obviously the players you're playing with.

“I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning, but I feel like when you get thrown in the deep end, it's the best way to learn. It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on.”

His recent deployment on the left wing has also offered another opportunity to broaden his game. Although not a position he has traditionally occupied, Osmand is relishing the licence to express himself.

“I’m really enjoying it. It's a really fun position and it's very, very attacking,” he commented. “I have a lot of freedom and the staff give me that freedom and tell me to go and try and make something happen. It's a great feeling when you know you can just go and impose your game.”

#1902. England squad controversy: Thomas Tuchel explains Cole Palmer absence as "desperate" Premier League star ahead of Chelsea man

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 15:18

England boss Thomas Tuchel has revealed that Cole Palmer has been left out of his squad for the November international break because he has missed too many chances to impress.

Premier League football will pause after this weekend so that Nations League fixtures can take place, and the Three Lions have named their 25-man squad.

Chelsea attacker Palmer has once again been left out by Tuchel, though he has called up Fulham forward Josh King, who plays in a similar position.

Speaking to reporters, Tuchel argued that Palmer has often missed the chance to impress, saying: "We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together.

"We have Josh King as a new player in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He is kind of an extra player and he can play all four positions. I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

"We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress."

Palmer was left out of England's squad for their games in early autumn, and he will play no part against either Croatia on November 12 or Spain on November 15.

Palmer has undoubtedly proven more at the top level of football than the likes of Morgan Gibbs-White and King, with the attacker even scoring in the Euro 2024 final.

However, the Englishman has been disappointing for Chelsea for some time, especially when playing against the division's best teams.

The 24-year-old has registered just five goal involvements in his last 19 league appearances against the Premier League's big six.

It should also be noted that Palmer has scored just four non-penalty goals in his last 26 games for Chelsea, and given his poor performance levels, he cannot be surprised to have been left out of the England squad.

King has been in exceptional form for Fulham this season, with the attacker playing out wide on the right and in a more central role.

The 19-year-old has scored once and assisted twice despite the struggles of his team, and his confidence will have been boosted thanks to Tuchel's decision to include him in his squad.

Exactly the same can be said for winger Rio Ngumoha, who was selected by Tuchel to play in England's friendlies prior to the World Cup, and becoming accustomed to the national team now could bode well for their chances of playing at Euro 2028.
