#1899. Man United Confidential: Club on red alert to prevent repeat of shocking Roma violence, why football insiders doubt Unai Emery is right fit for Old Trafford and meet the 17-year-old lighting up Darren Fletcher's impressive youth team

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 09:07 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 09:16 EDT, 3 November 2026

Manchester United are on high alert to prevent Roma fans infiltrating the areas of Old Trafford reserved for home supporters in tonight’s Champions League clash.

The fixture has a history of violence and United are determined to make sure more trouble isn’t sparked by Italian ultras buying tickets in the United sections of the stadium.

There were flashpoints when Galatasaray visited Old Trafford in October 2023, and again when Rangers were in town last year after tickets fell into the wrong hands.

There were concerns that the risk of unrest might be heightened by tickets for recent United games going on general sale, but the club insist they are only allocated to fans who were on their database prior to the Champions League draw being made.

The same restrictions apply to supporters forwarding season tickets and all hospitality guests whose tickets have been checked individually before being issued.

However, United will be extra vigilant to prevent Roma fans ending up among the home supporters, with any stray travelling fans being ejected immediately.

The rivalry between United and Roma dates back to their first meeting in April 2007 when Italian riot police were widely criticised for wading into English fans

United won the return leg of the quarter-final 7-1, with police making 18 arrests after fans clashed outside Old Trafford

The official allocation for the Italian club is 3,300, and those fans will congregate at Shambles Square in the city centre before making their way to Old Trafford under close police supervision.

Confidential understands Roma have avoided trouble playing away in Serie A and Europe this season after the Italian football authorities restricted travel for most of their teams.

With the exception of their games against Como and Udinese, Roma have only been allowed to take fans who live outside the Lazio region and are more likely to be affiliated to official fan clubs than the hardcore ultras who live in the centre of Rome.

The rivalry between United and Roma dates back to their first meeting in the quarter-final of the Champions League in April 2007 when Italian riot police were widely criticised for wading into English fans after they reacted to being pelted with missiles by Roma supporters.

A number of United fans were hospitalised, including 10 who were stabbed after being ambushed outside the Stadio Olimpico before kick-off. Roma were fined £31,000 – twice as much as United – and The Independent Manchester United Supporters’ Association pursued legal action against the Italian police for years afterwards.

United won the return leg 7-1, with police making 18 arrests after fans clashed outside Old Trafford. Sir Alex Ferguson’s side knocked Roma out of the quarter-finals again the following season on their way to winning the Champions League, having also played each other in the group stage – when trouble flared in Rome and three fans were stabbed.

Wayne Rooney scores United's third goal in that 7-1 thrashing. Michael Carrick also got on the scoresheet twice

The most recent meeting between the two clubs, in the Europa League semi-final in 2021, was played behind closed doors due to Covid.

A GMP spokesperson said: 'Greater Manchester Police is expecting a number of Roma supporters arriving into Manchester today with officers at the airport and would like to offer a warm welcome to all supporters.

'We are highly experienced in policing high-profile events and have been working closely with both clubs and supporters to ensure everyone can enjoy the match safely. We understand the majority of supporters attend matches peacefully however if there are any issues of disorder, we have a full plan in place to deal with concerns and will take action appropriately.

'There will be police in and around Old Trafford, so if you have any concerns before, during or after the match, then please speak to officers or stewards.'

The United squad flew back from London after Saturday’s defeat by Chelsea, avoiding the rail chaos that piled more misery onto their suffering fans.

Michael Carrick and the players took the train from Stockport to Euston on Friday, but returned by plane following the 2-0 loss. They were back at Carrington and heading for home by the time many supporters were left stranded by widespread delays caused by a points failure at Camden.

Confidential understands only one train left Euston for Manchester on Saturday evening and that was rammed with passengers desperate to get home and avoid having to pay for a hotel stay.

British Transport Police had to intervene to calm several disturbances before the train left Euston after standing still on the platform for half an hour, finally arriving at Manchester Piccadilly well after midnight.

Carrick and his players had a miserable time at Stamford Bridge on Saturday - but they did at least avoid the train chaos that affected the club's fans

When it comes to Ineos and the footballing decisions at United, much is made about the ‘best in class’ structure they have supposedly put in place.

There is Jason Wilcox as director of football, Christopher Vivell as director of recruitment, with figures like Michael Sansoni, director of data, key to the Ineos eco-system at Old Trafford. Omar Berrada is CEO and Sir Jim Ratcliffe is very hands-on as minority owner.

Carrick slotted into that set-up as head coach without ruffling any feathers. Should he get the boot, it’s fair to question if the structure is actually fit for purpose.

Chatting to Confidential in recent days, sources in the game explained why the current structure would not necessarily suit someone like Unai Emery.

As one of the best managers in the Premier League, Emery should be a dream target if United are to move on from Carrick in the coming weeks. He is, it is understood, on a five-man shortlist of potential replacements.

But Aston Villa boss Emery, for example, is said to choose his own sporting director and deal directly with ownership – rather than a director of football or a CEO – given the immense power he wields.

Would Unai Emery be happy to work with the likes of Omar Berrada (left) and Jason Wilcox?

There are serious questions being asked of Wilcox and Berrada right now. What happens moving forward with Vivell is also an issue.

Which raises the question: if United pivot in the dugout in a bid to save this sorry season and they have any chance of landing a big fish like Emery, why would you stick to a system that wouldn’t be agreeable to one of the league’s very best managers?

Maybe the structure is the problem, after all.

It’s approaching half a century since United’s famous win over Liverpool in the 1977 FA Cup final denied Bob Paisley’s side the chance of winning the Treble, but the rivalry has paid off for the family of Emlyn Hughes.

When the two clubs met again at Wembley later that summer and shared the Charity Shield after a goalless draw, Liverpool’s captain and No 6 swapped shirts with his United counterpart Martin Buchan whose white Admiral jersey with the three vertical stripes sold for £10,000 at auction on Monday.

The shirt, which had an estimate of between £4-6,000, was one of 200 lots from Hughes’ career with Liverpool, Wolves and England which were auctioned off by Budds on behalf of his family. A Northern Ireland No 8 jersey worn by George Best also sold for £49,000.

Hughes, who died in 2004 at the age of 57, led the great Liverpool side that would have beaten United by 22 years to become the first English club to win the league title, European Cup and FA Cup in the same season were it not for Tommy Docherty’s team, captained by Buchan, beating them 2-1.

Almost 50 years later, the rivalry between the two clubs is still as strong as ever as United prepare to go to Anfield straight after the international break.

Finding slivers of positivity at United right now is far from easy, but Darren Fletcher’s Under 18s are doing their level best as their 10-game unbeaten run goes on.

Spearheaded by Kai Rooney, Noah Ajayi and Jaume Camacho, Fletcher’s fledglings have hit 38 goals in the past 10 games, scoring 16 in the past three alone with a 6-3 win over Liverpool followed up by a 6-0 win at Burnley and a 4-1 win at Blackburn.

Jaume Camacho, 17, is a real rising star and helping Darren Fletcher's Under 18s play some scintillating football

This was a squad overshadowed by the brilliance of JJ Gabriel last season and one that started this campaign without too much star power on paper.

But with Camacho, 17, a real rising star – his four goals against Liverpool were sublime – Fletcher’s side are playing some top football and dismantling teams the way other clubs are dismantling United's first team right now.

United have 99 problems, but Fletcher’s Under 18s aren’t one.

#1898. Ten FA Cup first-round memories to recall from Yorkshire's non-league clubs since 2000

For lower-division EFL clubs suddenly cast as 'Goliath', there have also been some unwanted recent round-one memories. The names Tamworth and King's Lynn will send a shiver down the spines of Huddersfield Town and Doncaster Rovers, for instance.

And what about the plain bizarre? Just mention Horsham to Barnsley, infamously kicked out of the Cup in November 2023 for fielding an ineligible player in a first-round replay win in West Sussex.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Back in the 1980s and 90s, the likes of Frickley Athletic and Emley took centre stage on the giant-killing front in the county. This century, it has been the turn of others. Some have been fortunate enough to make round two and while others haven't, the fact that they announced themselves on the map, albeit briefly, provided kudos and pride for being part of the rich FA Cup story.

As non-leaguers Harrogate Town, Halifax and Guiseley aim to make more memories today, here’s ten first-round moments to recall since 2000.

2023: Scarborough Athletic 2 Forest Green 4

Rovers held off non-league Boro in a frenetic replayed tie to set up a trip to Blackpool in round two - in front of a crowd of over 2,500.

The Football Association ordered the match to be replayed after a mix-up regarding a loan player's eligibility to play for the League Two club in the original tie, which ended 1-1 before Rovers won the 'replay' 5-2.

Ryan Qualter gave the hosts a shock lead, before the visitors turned the tables to lead 3-1. Luca Colville gave Jono Greening's side hope in their quest to force extra-time before Rovers scored a killer fourth.

2021: FC Halifax Town 7 Maidenhead United 4

Six different home players struck to ensure that the Shaymen prevailed on an astonishing afternoon against their National League rivals, courtesy of goals from Billy Waters (2), Tyrell Warren, Matty Warburton, Kian Spence, Jordan Slew and Elliot Newby.

'Sublime to the ridiculous' was Halifax chief Pete Wild's astute post-match verdict on events.

The Lions withstood a dramatic late comeback from their League Two opponents to reach the second round for just the second time ever.

The Nethermoor action saw Will Hatfield put the hosts ahead with a sweet half-volley and a Cliff Moyo cross-shot made it 2-0 at the break.

Strikes from Kaine Felix and Kingsley James put Guiseley in dreamland by the midway point of the second half - the prelude to a storming U's fightback, with Jabo Ibehre (2) and George Maris netting.

Unfortunately, chairman Gary Douglas was en route to Hong Kong and missed witnessing Guiseley's big day.

2017: Shaw Lane Aquaforce 1 Mansfield Town 3

Barnsley-based Evo-Stik Premier League side Shaw Lane, who were a Sunday League side until 2011, were undone by a fine second-half brace from Barnsley-born Danny Rose, who lived a few streets away from the hosts' stadium.

Earlier, Grimethorpe lad Lee Bennett had cancelled out Krystian Pearce's Stags opener - in the biggest game in the club's history.

Shaw Lane goalkeeper Jon Stewart saved a penalty from ex-Reds midfielder Jacob Mellis.

Two goals in four minutes helped Bradford edge past the Shaymen in front of more than 8,000 fans at The Shay.

Lois Maynard gave Halifax a shock early lead and they held their precious advantage for 50 minutes.

But the half-time introduction of Billy Clarke turned the game as he set up Jon Stead and Filipe Morais as City struck twice in four minutes.

Chib Chilaka was Harrogate's hero, firing a famous winner at Plainmoor for Simon Weaver's Blue Square Bet North side on 19 minutes.

It represented the first time in the Sulphurites' history that they progressed beyond the first round.

The closest they had previously come was ironically against Torquay in 2005, when the Gulls won on penalties after a replay.

Conference North part-timers Celtic earned a replay following a gripping draw at Throstle Nest.

Simeon Bambrook and Roy Starmer went close, while Ryan Crossley also saw a header cleared off the line. MK won the replay 2-0.

2003: Bradford (Park Avenue) 2 Bristol City 5

No progression for Avenue, but a key milestone as it marked their return to the national stage for the first time since reformation in 1988.

A crowd of just under 2,000 roared on the hosts at the Horsfall Stadium. Four goals were shared in an incredible opening 13 minutes as the hosts gave the Robins a real scare. Andy Hayward netted for the hosts, while City’s Dan Coles scored an own goal in the televised tie.

Northern Counties East Premier Division side Railway pulled off a shock win at their Ryman Division One hosts.

Slough led through a Byron Bubb free-kick. But the visitors levelled in the second half when the Slough defence failed to clear an Ian McLean free-kick and Kevin Smith headed home. McLean also set up the winner, headed in by Steve Davey.

The Match of the Day cameras saw the Seasiders draw 1-1 at the Turnbull Ground and give Argyle a real fright.

Whitby shocked the Pilgrims by opening the scoring three minutes before half-time when Alex Gildea converted Jamie Burt’s cross.

Argyle levelled on 72 minutes, with Martin Phillips ending the defiance of home keeper Phil Naisbett. They won the replay 3-2.

The money Whitby accrued from the tie was already earmarked for ground repairs and the club issued an appeal for cash to fund the 765-round-trip to Home Park for the midweek replay. Peter Ridsdale, then chairman at Leeds United, duly obliged, paying for the travel costs alongside an overnight hotel stay.

#1897. Napoli vs Lazio - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 06 Nov 2026 15:25, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 15:29

Trending in very different directions, Serie A leaders Lazio will visit a faltering Napoli side on Sunday, as Stadio Maradona hosts the lunchtime kickoff.

While the home side are struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, their southern rivals have posted nine wins from 10 and are yet to taste defeat in the league.

Sparking crisis talks between the coaching staff and club president Aurelio Di Laurentiis, Napoli are in danger of missing this season's objectives with several months left to play.

On Wednesday night, the Partenopei suffered a chastening 4-1 defeat to Porto, meaning they have lost seven of their last eight Champions League away games. Having finished 30th in the 36-team table last term, they currently sit 27th - inside the elimination zone.

A former finalist with Juventus, head coach Massimiliano Allegri has personally lost nine of his last 11 matches at Europe's elite level, and he is also under pressure for some dire domestic results.

Napoli lie eighth in Serie A after last week's 2-0 defeat to Juve, and with a 14-point deficit to surprise leaders Lazio they are surely out of the title race.

Defeat this weekend would result in their worst start since 2007, and Allegri cannot expect any favours from his former midfield general at AC Milan.

While Gennaro Gattuso has lost all five of their meetings in management, recent events suggest that trend could soon end.

Including a frantic 3-3 draw in the Derby del Sole, Napoli have gone six games without a clean sheet while conceding 13 goals, and they must now host Roma's fierce city rivals.

Precedent is certainly on Lazio's side, having won on all of their last four visits to Naples and prevailed in five of the last eight meetings overall.

More pertinently, the capital club have just won six consecutive Serie A games, leaving their more optimistic fans dreaming of a first Scudetto since the 1999-2000 campaign.

Gattuso will not be drawn on such talk, even though his side boast the division's joint-best defensive record and have scored at least twice in their last eight matches.

This century, only four teams have previously hit 28 points after 10 matchdays, and that tally has lifted them three clear of reigning champions Inter Milan.

Along the way, Lazio have also had 12 different goalscorers, with Gustav Isaksen finding the net four times in his last five appearances.

The Danish winger was on target in last week's 2-1 win over Cagliari, as the Biancocelesti capitalised on Inter's Milan derby defeat and took sole possession of top spot.

Now, Gattuso will return to a club where he won the Coppa Italia but was subsequently sacked, seeking an incredible sixth straight away win in Serie A.

Adding to the sense of crisis in Naples, Allegri has been hampered by a long injury list for several weeks.

Alessandro Buongiorno, David Neres, Costantino Favasuli, Alisson Santos, Leonardo Spinazzola, Benoit Badiashile and Stanislav Lobotka are all unavailable, while two full-backs are facing a race against time.

Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Mathias Olivera both sustained muscular injuries last weekend, when Luca Marianucci was sent off against Juventus and incurred a one-match ban.

Despite his advancing years and chequered fitness history, Kevin De Bruyne may be asked to go again, having scored three goals in his last five league games.

Without Europe to consider, Gattuso has made relatively few changes so far, and it should be a settled Lazio side that takes to the field on Sunday.

However, he will have to replace captain Mattia Zaccagni, who could be ruled out until next month with a thigh strain.

Albert Gudmundsson is still sidelined after dislocating his shoulder on Iceland duty, but with Adam Marusic and Nicolo Rovella finally back in full training, everyone else should be available.

Meret; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, De Bruyne, McTominay, Vergara; Giovane, Hojlund

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Sutalo, Provstgaard, Tavares; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin

Struggling in Serie A, facing another early exit from Europe and burdened by a huge absence list, Napoli are set to lose three games on the spin.

While Lazio's stellar run will surely end soon, they can exploit their hosts' shaky defence and post a seventh straight win.

#1896. GdS: Milan’s €500m Adidas deal causes reaction from rivals Inter – the situation

Inter are looking enviously at their city rivals AC Milan once again after Saturday’s derby, with the news of the record Adidas deal emerging.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport on Wednesday, under the new agreement Adidas will pay Milan €50m per year for ten seasons starting from 2028-29. This is when the collaboration with PUMA ends, who currently pay €24.5m per year, as per the last accounts.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The paper (via Calciomercato.com) go on to state that it is likely that the €50m yearly figure includes sporting bonuses, such as participation in the Champions League, the value of material supplies (value in kind) and a portion to be invested in promotional activities (marketing fund).

Contracts with kit makers are not limited to recognising the value of just the home, away, third and other shirts, but can extend to the sale of related products. Then, guaranteed minimums and royalties come into play that are triggered above a certain turnover threshold.

For example, in addition to the €24.5m from PUMA, €55.8m in revenues came from store, e-commerce and merchandising/licensing activities, in particular those relating to the contract with the same German company and those from licensing with Fanatics and MatchWornShirt.

As for Inter, the renewal with Nike – effective from 2023 – resulted in a 70% increase over the previous contract, but the €28m per year is not in line with the club’s current commercial value. In addition to the Milan-Adidas deal, Juventus currently get €46m per year from Adidas (€41m from 2027-28).

Inter have maintained their merchandising revenues internally, over €35m in 2025-26 thanks to the new business model introduced with Fanatics, but Nike’s €28m is too little according to the Nerazzurri’s commercial management.

The contract expires in 2031, and La Gazzetta report that they will seek to renegotiate the deal to avoid accumulating delays over the next five years. Considering that Juventus and Milan have committed to the next decade, Inter have leverage as the only one of the ‘big three’ up for grabs.

#1895. Guiseley v Sutton United: Juggling FA Cup and league is not an issue for Lions

Just over a year after the PE teacher took charge at Nethermoor Park, the Lions are third in the Northern Premier League Premier Division. Beating Sutton United on Saturday goes hand in hand with the league.

It is easy to see why Richards is such a fan of the world's most famous domestic cup competition.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"I don't like 'This isn't our priority this year,'" says Richards. "I might make a couple of changes with personnel, but we've built a squad where one in, one out, the quality doesn't change.

"We've had a county cup game within this (period between the qualifying rounds and Saturday) and played a team three leagues below us, but I still took a strong side. We won that 4-0. It's really important to get a clean sheet.

"We had a game against Leek Town on Tuesday in the league, and in line with the laws, they said they would postpone it if we wished. But we wanted to play it.

"It could have easily been one where players were subconsciously or consciously not at it 100 per cent. We ran out comfortable 4-1 winners and managed to get all five subs on. We came out with no new injuries.

"The players are in really good form. We've won eight and drawn one of our last nine games."

The Football Association have put attractive prize money into the early stages of their blue riband competition, giving something for romantics and pragmatists to play for. Victory on Saturday is worth £47,750, but even losing will bring in £15,800, and there is minimum prize money of £21,200 in round two.

"We're expecting a big crowd," said Richards. "There's never been that pressure from the club, but we have to be aware of prize money. If you want to improve the ground or reinvest in the squad, it's excellent.

"We got 1,600 at the (third qualifying round) Bradford (Park Avenue) game. "Then we played Leiston away and even though the gate money wasn't huge, it did give us publicity.

"And it's memories for the players. When I was at Halifax Town I got as far as the second round (in 1999). We lost in a replay to Reading. I remember Darren Caskey scoring the penalty at the Madejski Stadium, which was very new.

"As a manager, I've taken my two previous clubs (Stocksbridge Park Steels and Penistone Church) the furthest they've ever been in the FA Cup. The players still talk about that.

"I think this is the 11th time in Guiseley’s 117-year history they've got to the first round. They've only got to the second round twice and they were a National League side.

"Hopefully if there's new supporters coming, they may come back for two, three, four more games.

"There's a backlog of games, but winning builds momentum."

Playing a South London team from the Conference brings challenges for a part-time club, but nothing Richards is afraid of.

"I'm doing my research on Sutton," he says. "We'll train as we would do for any other game. But there'll be over 2,000 watching so we've got to use that as a motivation.

"Our head of football watches as many games as he can, so he went to Sutton against Harrogate Town. I've not been able to watch them live but I've got plenty of footage.

"They've got some real pace and power in wide areas. They've got good footballers in attacking midfield, but they are quite direct.

"Their pitch is an excellent surface, so they do try and play when they can, but they're quite happy to go forward very quickly.

"If I was playing a team two leagues below, I'd try and play on the front foot so we'll expect them to get the ball forward quickly and really commit numbers forward."

"We get school holidays, so that's the time I spend with my family," he says. "When you're doing well, it can get even busier, but I can't complain.

"I'm the vice-principal at Penistone Grammar School and I teach A-Level PE. It's my 12th year.

"I live in a little village called Shepley. We train at Lightcliffe Academy, about half-an-hour away.

"Midweek games are a bit of a nightmare with traffic, but my coach lives around the corner and my assistant lives in Thorpe Hesley so we're always travelling together.

"My pupils aren't fully aware of Guiseley but know the level it's at and what I do. We also have a number of teaching staff who follow non-league football. A few are going."

And whenever this run ends, it will be back to pushing for promotion from the seventh tier. They are three points behind leaders Redcar Athletic with a game in hand.

"When we took over at the end of October (2025), they were out of every competition and third from bottom," recalls Richards. "My objective was, at this stage, to be in every competition and above two points per game and we've achieved that.

"Only one goes up automatically but there are now six play-off places. We've got to make sure iIf we don't win it, we fall into a high play-off position."

Then this experience of knockout football will come in handy.

"With my previous clubs, we won promotions in the play-offs," he points out. "Even though at the time you're not thinking about it, I can reference the cup wins as I give my teamtalk.

"It's a long season, so every little bit helps."

#1893. FC Twente vs Ajax - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 06 Nov 2026 16:02

The standout fixture of gameweek 12 in the 2026-27 Eredivisie campaign sees FC Twente and Ajax face off at De Grolsch Veste.

Both teams begin Sunday’s heavyweight clash inside the top four, with the possibility that one could finish the weekend at the summit.

Just four days after recording their biggest-ever league win away at SBV Excelsior in a 9-0 thrashing, Twente faced a more demanding continental test against Pafos on Thursday, coming from behind to claim a 3-1 victory in their third Conference League outing.

One of three teams still boasting a perfect record in Europe’s third-tier competition, Trots van het Oosten are in pole position to reach the knockout stages of a UEFA tournament for the first time since 2011, continuing to make waves in their first full season under John van den Brom.

Riding their joint-longest winning run in over three years, Twente now face arguably their toughest test of the campaign so far. Emerging unscathed would only intensify the growing whispers of a potential title challenge.

The Tukkers have beaten this weekend’s opponent just once in the last five meetings, though that victory came in the most recent clash back in April, when Ramiz Zerrouki and Bart van Rooy netted to seal a 2-1 win.

With only 10 goals conceded - the fewest in the division - a newfound defensive solidity has underpinned Twente’s success so far. It also helps that they have been quick starters, scoring first in eight of their last nine league outings.

Ajax were also in Conference League action in midweek, running riot against Danish side Midtjylland with a 6-1 thrashing at the MCH Arena, picking up where they left off in their last league outing against AZ Alkmaar.

That marked a fifth consecutive victory, as Michel’s men have wasted no time in bouncing back from a three-match winless run either side of the September/October international break - a spell that threatened to derail their ambitions for the season.

Currently the only Eredivisie side with a perfect away record, De Godenzonen now head to Enschede aiming to stay within touching distance of leaders Feyenoord, who could be five points clear by the time proceedings get underway in Twente.

Up against the league’s top scorer, Wout Weghorst, and the leading assist provider, Sondre Orjasaeter, Ajax have their work cut out in their quest for consecutive victories at De Grolsch Veste for the first time since 2021.

Like their hosts, Sunday’s visitors have delivered the first blow more often than not lately - breaking the deadlock in each of their last five outings - and will hope it continues in a fixture whose last six editions have seen them concede the opener five times.

Stav Lemkin (muscle) has yet to feature for Twente this season and is ruled out on Sunday, alongside fellow defender Max Bruns.

First-choice goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall remains sidelined, so Joel Drommel should make a ninth consecutive start between the sticks.

Twenty-year-old Filip Thorvaldsen has endured an injury-hit debut campaign and is once again out of contention for the hosts.

Ajax are contending with a lengthy injury list, with up to eight players potentially missing this weekend’s clash.

Caio Henrique and Anton Gaaei are significant absentees at the back, while the loss of Sofyan Amrabat and Julian Brandt further limits Ajax’s midfield options.

Viktor Tsygankov, Simon Adingra, Kasper Dolberg, and Oliver Valaker Edvardsen remain unavailable in attack, meaning leading scorer Tolu Arokodare is unlikely to be rested after his brace against Midtjylland.

Drommel; Van Rooy, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Weidmann; Rots, Taha, Orjasaeter; Weghorst

Ter Stegen; Wijndal, Janse, Bouwman, Rosa; Baas, Mokio; Gloukh, Klaassen, Ouazane; Arokodare

Given the strong form of both sides, Sunday’s clash could go either way and is difficult to call.

As a result, we are leaning towards a share of the spoils, with honours even at the full-time whistle.

#1892. Jermain Defoe could make dugout comeback four months after abrupt Woking departure - as ex-Premier League star is mooted as potential assistant to Karl Robinson at Bromley

Published: 11:36 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 11:47 EDT, 3 November 2026

Former Salford City manager Karl Robinson is in the running for the Bromley job and could be joined in the dugout by a Premier League icon.

Daily Mail Sport understands that former Tottenham striker Jermain Defoe, most recently Woking manager, has been discussed as a potential assistant should Robinson be appointed to fill the vacancy left by Andy Woodman, who was dismissed last month.

Defoe left Woking after less than four months following a breakdown in his relationship with the club's director of football.

His departure came in dramatic circumstances, failing to turn up for training on the eve of the new season before calling the club to say he would not be returning.

Robinson previously tried to sign Defoe on a free transfer after he left Scottish club Rangers while Oxford United manager.

Defoe played 496 Premier League games, spread across six clubs, scoring 163 goals.

Jermain Defoe (right) could return to coaching soon as potential assistant manager of Bromley

He is Tottenham's seventh-highest all-time goalscorer and ranks 10th on the Premier League's all-time scoring list.

Having failed to land Defoe as a player, Robinson could yet get his man in management.

Bromley have been assessing several candidates as their managerial search enters its second week.

They have already held talks with Chelsea legend Ashley Cole, who took charge of Serie B club Cesena for three months at the end of last season, while former Oxford United boss Matt Bloomfield is in the frame. Cole was previously assistant manager of England Under-21s.

The Ravens sit bottom of League One and are winless in six matches.

Woodman was sacked after five years in charge, having led Bromley from the National League to League One, with just two wins in ten matches in their maiden season in the third tier.

Speaking on the Inside the 72 podcast this week, Woodman said: 'You have to speak honestly. The easiest way I can sum this up is that when I got the job at Bromley, my first game was Wealdstone and my last game in the league was Leicester.

'I'm pretty disappointed, pretty upset and feel pretty misled in numerous ways and situations.

Defoe could join former Salford City manager Karl Robinson if he takes over at the club

'To give five and a half years of my life to a club and a fan base that I really loved and bought into and gave everything I had and be told in no less than four minutes, thanks, that was it really.

'There's no other way of dressing this up. I'm disappointed but that's football as we know it. Unfortunately, it never surprises me.'

Byron Webster, who made 173 appearances in six years at Bromley, is currently in interim charge at the south-east London club.

Away from footballing matters, former Everton striker and cult hero Victor Anichebe is in the final stages of completing a takeover at Bromley. Anichebe is understood to be involved in the search for a new manager.

For Drury, pitting his wits against the very best at a tactical level particularly inspires him. He also sees a cup run as something which can dovetail with his side's fine league form, viewing it as a help not a hindrance.

"We want to go far in the competition. We want to progress. We want to continue doing what we're doing as a group and continuing our performances and developing our performances."

As a football fan, Drury has his own special memories of the competition, having attended the famous Steel City semi-final at the old Wembley between Sheffield United and Sheffield Wednesday in 1993.

#1887. Man United transfer news: Michael Carrick faces 'exciting' £23m battle with Chelsea and Arsenal for midfielder

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 16:14

Manchester United will have to battle the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea for Galatasaray midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, the latest report has claimed.

The Red Devils are readying themselves for their final game before the start of the November international break, with the club set to welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford on Sunday.

A defeat could leave the team in the Premier League's relegation zone, and that would almost certainly lead to the dismissal of Michael Carrick.

United's struggles this campaign can in part be explained by the fact their midfield has performed poorly all season, including newcomer Carlos Baleba, who is now set for a period on the sidelines due to a hamstring injury.

It should come as no surprise to see the club linked to more midfielders, though TEAMtalk report that if United are to sign Galatasaray's Batrakov, they may have to convince the Russian to join them ahead of Arsenal and Chelsea.

Valued by Transfermarkt at just over £23m, Batrakov is unlikely to command a significant fee given he has never played in any of Europe's top five leagues.

The midfielder has performed excellently for Galatasaray, scoring five goals while providing three assists in 12 games for the club this season.

Four of those goals came in the Champions League, with the 21-year-old netting twice against Stuttgart, once against Lille and once against Barcelona.

Batrakov can play as either a number eight or an attacking midfielder, though he is arguably at his best when allowed to charge into the penalty area, so perhaps he could be seen as a replacement for Bruno Fernandes.

However, asking him to come to England and step into the void that could be left by the club's captain would be risky, and he should not be relied upon as a starter.

United should not be in a position where they need to sign yet another midfielder after signing three last summer.

It is alarming that co-owners INEOS, who reportedly have control over sporting decisions at Old Trafford, are seemingly admitting that their midfield revamp was a failure.

The Red Devils will also need to rebuild their defence over the next two transfer windows, while there are concerns about the level of their attack, so it remains to be seen if United will be able to fill the holes in their squad.

#1886. Oldham Athletic v Sheffield Wednesday: 'Show us what you have got' is Dave Challinor's message to Owls

Dave Challinor has done plenty of talking in his first week as Sheffield Wednesday manager, and when the action starts at Boundary Park on Sunday evening, the message to his new players is clear.

The 51-year-old has had his first week on the Middlewood Road training pitches, and now he is anxious to see how his new players put it into practice in the FA Cup first round at Oldham Athletic.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"I'm really looking forward to it, more as my first real eyes on from a dugout position," said the former Colwyn Bay, Fylde, Hartlepool United and Stockport County manager.

"There will be information we've given the players and we want to see how they can carry those things out.

"We know between now and Christmas the run of games we have got of Saturday-Tuesdays and we go against some of the sides you would expect to compete for promotion.

"We have to hit the ground running. We've got to continue to develop whilst winning.

"The players I won't say have been bombarded. We have to prioritise the bits that are important.

"There are things that have been in place that are good and we have to make sure we continue to improve on those things but just add bits.

"It won't be immediate change, it'll be constant over the next couple of weeks.

"We have done quite a bit without going into too much detail. I hope you will see in the first game the changes that we want to look at.

"We've got a really good group of players and we need to try to facilitate their best bits on a football pitch, regardless of the opposition. That's what we'll try and do."

Challinor's job is to try and learn about his squad.

"I will speak to all the players," he said. "Everyone has different drivers, different markers.

"But if you can't enjoy being a footballer at Sheffield Wednesday, especially when you're at home in front of 30,000 people – I'd worry for you.

"Will there be some mistakes? Of course there will. But I'm really intrigued to see what they've got from the start from a pitchside, from a dugout perspective.

"I've got true belief that we'll produce a performance befitting of everything that happens on Sunday in terms of the travelling supporters."

He needs professional pride to be a factor in the 5.15pm TNT Sports game at League Two Oldham.

"They're a little bit up and down in terms of results," said Challinor. "They had a good result on Tuesday going to Northampton and winning.

"It's the FA Cup. From our side of things I don't imagine playing on a Sunday at 5.15 would have been the case if they'd have thought it was a synch and a walkover.

"We've got to go and be Sheffield Wednesday, that's the most important thing for us.

"We've got really good players, they need to perform for ourselves and for the supporters – undoubtedly we'll have a full away end – and show what we're about.

"There's been things said about the team recently that aren't nice. Use that as a motivation."

Di’Shon Bernard is available having has trained all week, but the bulk of the Owls' injured players will not be back until next week's league game at home to Plymouth Argyle, which now looks set to go ahead. Liam Cooper, Joe Lumley and Ali Al-Hamadi could feature then.

"They're probably not too far away in terms of being back in training to a certain degree," said Challinor.

"We've got the midweek fixture against Accrington (in the EFL Trophy). We have to plan. It's not something you'd ideally do in November, but that's where we are."

For now, that might mean players having to play out of position.

"That's probably going to be the case for the next few weeks," warns Challinor.

"You would love to put people into positions where they are comfortable but that's not always the case that you can do it.

"There's been plenty of adversity over the course of the season with injuries, suspensions and all them things and that continues because we've still got players out but we can't use that as an excuse.

"We hope over the next couple of weeks it will get better because we'll get numbers back which will allow us more options as players back from injury and I would expect that we'll get stronger and stronger."

Sil Swinkels is suspended after his red card against Blackpool.

Will Grainger will miss next week's games after being selected by Wales for their European Under-19s Championship qualifiers against Finland, Spain and Iceland.

Sunday's game will be played to a finish, with extra time and penalties to decide who goes into Monday's draw.

#1885. Arsenal v Hull City: Sergej Jakirovic's plans A, B and C to avoid another nightmare against Europe's elite

His Tigers take on Arsenal side who he regards as one of the two best teams in Europe on their own patch in Saturday's Premier League.

He has come up against Europe’s elite before, and found out the hard way how tough it can be.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Jakirovic was coach of Dinamo Zagreb when they faced Bayern Munich in the 2024-25 Champions League group stage and was on the wrong end of a 9-2 defeat which saw him sacked two days later.

At the time it was the biggest victory in Champions League history, although Como outdid that with Tuesday's 9-1 win at Lens.

"Especially this night, we were not at this level at all, and if you are not compact, if you are shuffling, especially when they try to play around you to pull you out of your position, they will use all these gaps between your players, because they recognise this immediately," said Jakirovic.

"In that game they had three penalties (all scored by Harry Kane), which is a little bit weird, but they will use every mistake, they will punish you, they will not miss their opportunities.

"We tried something this week. We tried everything – plan A, plan B, even C.

"But you don't have a chance if you sit back like 5-4-1 and if you are passive, they will destroy you.

"It has to be front foot, it has to be aggressive on the body especially because they have a very high quality in their roster.

"You can be more solid, more aggressive, especially in the challenge, especially the second goal against Ipswich (in last week's 2-1 defeat). We could stop this easily, we can make a foul at least. At this level, it's a goal.

"Arsenal are playing very good football, no matter Champions League or Premier League. They are very strong, they control everything not just against us, also other better clubs.

"Obviously, they are a big favourite, and we can start to try to create some difficulties for them."

Fortunately, Hull have already shown this season and last they are made of tough stuff if they concd arly.

"You need to be really mentally strong if this happens," said the former Bosnia player.

"Every goal is very important, especially for the goal difference, and also we have to show mentality like we always do.

"We already had this experience – Chelsea away game, Newcastle away – but we should try to avoid this 100 per cent.

"Our mental resilience is very important because of everything we did in the past – this team, together, chemistry, togetherness, team spirit, everything. So this is the main thing we have."

Asked what he would talk to Mikel Arteta about if he shares a drink with the Gunners manager at full-time, Jakirovic replied: "I will ask him to give me his budget!

"But he deserves to be at this level. He was (a coach) at Man City, now he's been at Arsenal (as manager) almost seven years, and it's progress every year.

"It's not easy to build a new team, but you have options to add more quality in your team, because Arsenal is a top-five team in Europe, in terms of everything.

"This a chance to show we can compete there. Maybe you can surprise them with something, and also you can compare where we are right now, because they are the best, it's not a secret."

#1884. Inter Milan vs Como - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 06 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 17:00

Having suffered derby defeat and slipped off top spot in Serie A, reigning champions Inter Milan must try to get back on track when they welcome record-breaking Como to San Siro on Sunday.

Following four intense meetings last term, the regional rivals are currently separated by two points, with both trailing surprise leaders Lazio.

Ending their 19-game undefeated streak in Serie A, Inter were well beaten by AC Milan in last week's Derby della Madonnina, making it eight straight second-city contests without a win.

With illness sweeping through Cristian Chivu's squad, those fit enough to start were swept aside by the rampant Rossoneri, who surged into an early two-goal lead and eventually won 3-1.

After falling three points behind Lazio, the Nerazzurri had little time to reflect and swiftly switched focus to their ailing European campaign.

Inter had claimed just three points from their opening three Champions League matches, but they were back near their best on Tuesday night, beating Feyenoord 3-0 at De Kuip.

Yann Bisseck put the visitors in front, and Pio Esposito doubled their lead before the break, with Piotr Zielinski adding an excellent third goal in the second half.

As a result, Chivu and co sit 14th in the table midway through this season's league phase, keeping them firmly in contention for the knockout rounds.

Before international football intervenes, they must now face a potential title rival - albeit one whom they have traditionally dominated.

History weighs heavily on Inter's side in this Lombardy derby, having won 14 consecutive Serie A home games against Como, while keeping a clean sheet in eight of the last nine.

Dating back down the decades, Como have lost their last 11 top-flight meetings with Inter, plus a recent Coppa Italia semi-final tie between the two sides.

Very much in demand, head coach Cesc Fabregas has come away empty-handed from each league game against a club that sought to appoint him in the summer of 2025.

Inter tried to lure the Catalan away from Como before hiring Chivu, but going toe-to-toe with the Nerazzurri has brought four straight Serie A defeats by a 12-3 aggregate scoreline.

That sequence includes a chastening 4-0 loss at San Siro last December, but the Biancoblu were unlucky not to reach the cup final after a thrilling semi-final second leg a few months later.

More recently, they have made Europe sit up and take notice with some eye-catching Champions League results, as the debutants followed their 4-1 defeat of Manchester United with a ruthless destruction of Lens.

Como travelled to France in midweek and left with an emphatic 9-1 victory, top scorer Tasos Douvikas helping himself to a hat-trick in an incredible rout.

That leaves the rookies above the likes of Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Inter in the table, with automatic entry to the last 16 now firmly fixed in their sights.

Since losing 3-2 to Feyenoord on matchday two, they have put together six consecutive wins across all competitions, scoring 22 goals and conceding just four.

In Serie A, the Lariani have collected a club record 23 points from their first 10 fixtures, and few would rule them out of vying for the Scudetto.

Though Inter captain Lautaro Martinez is not due back until after the break, and Luis Henrique is also ruled out, the hosts can welcome back a trio of players.

Benjamin Pavard has joined English pair John Stones and Curtis Jones in resuming full training, and they could all make the bench this weekend.

Furthermore, Alessandro Bastoni - who scored in last week's Milan derby - is available after serving a UEFA suspension against Feyenoord.

Up front, Pio Esposito has just netted his first club goal since September, while Marcus Thuram has previously scored four in three league games against Como.

The visitors also boast a potent attack, as Douvikas and star man Nico Paz already have nine Champions League strikes between them.

That pair have been similarly productive in Serie A, with 11 goal involvements combined, but Douvikas has failed to find the net in five prior games against Inter.

Once again, Fabregas will be without Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Jesus Rodriguez, Jayden Addai and Assane Diao due to injury.

J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Butez; Couto, Kempf, Ramon, Kaiki; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Inter's defence is creaking at the seams, and without the leadership of their inspirational skipper they are always more vulnerable.

Although free-flowing Como must be starting to tire, recent events suggest it is time to finally slay the Nerazzurri.

#1883. Bukayo Saka ‘a bit fragile,’ reckons former Arsenal and Manchester United defender

Bukayo Saka is ‘a bit fragile’ and must work on preventing injury problems in future, reckons former Arsenal defender Mikael Silvestre.

The Gunners winger is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem picked up in a Champions League clash with Bayern Munich on October 21.

Saka is not expected to be back in action until December, with Noni Madueke filling in on the right flank in his absence.

The 25-year-old has been hampered by some injury issues over the last two seasons, but has still managed to rack up a huge amount of appearances, 323 for Arsenal in total.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

He played 49 times in all competitions last season, although the 2024/25 campaign saw him play the least since he broke into the first team, turning out 37 times.

Silvestre accepts that injuries are bound to occur for players of Saka’s ilk, but suggests he is not quite as robust as he could be.

‘When you are an explosive player like Saka, obviously the muscles are what will trouble you when you are doing those sprints all the time,’ Silvestre told PariuriX.com. ‘Maybe, he is a bit fragile, and with the amount of games things like this can happen.

‘What is important for him is the recovery and the prevention, because it’s very important for him that it doesn’t happen too often, because he is very important for Arsenal.’

Silvestre sees Madueke as an improving force in Saka’s absence, although there is still room to become sharper in the final third.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘That’s why you have a big squad and Madueke would start for most of the teams in the Premier League, if not all,’ said the Frenchman. ‘He has the quality and I think he is getting his confidence now, he is trying to score and create more.

‘He doesn’t have the killer instinct yet, but he is growing into it and he is trying to get there.’

Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with Manchester United, reckons Arsenal’s forward line as a whole can let them down, with their strength clearly lying in defence. The recent 1-0 win at Liverpool being a good illustration.

‘Winning at Anfield, with a clean sheet as well makes it a very good defensive performance,’ he said. ‘We can’t say the same with the offense. I would say that’s one for the record, and one that you look back at the end of the season and say it was an important 3 points. But it wasn’t a full on, top class, 90 minute performance from Arsenal.

‘But it’s important to get those wins against teams who are also potentially in the race, and to keep your distance from them.

‘The positives are the defensive side of things, the 3 points, and the fact that it was at Anfield. It breaks that negative dynamic but I think it’s just for the stats really.

‘I think you need your best players at the key moments featuring in the semi-finals and the final of competitions. Arsenal need to keep Timber fit, Saliba is coming back also. You need your strong 11 and the best defence once you reach the final. So it’s still a long way away but they defend well, as a unit for sure.’

#1881. From Jose Mourinho's Sevilla disaster to Erik ten Hag's dismal group stage exit: Man United's litany of Champions League humiliations since Sir Alex Ferguson - as Michael Carrick fights for his job ahead of Roma clash

Published: 18:02 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EDT, 3 November 2026

Michael Carrick and Manchester United are enduring the club's worst start to a league season in 40 years, with the Red Devils languishing in 17th place.

Their woes in recent years have been well documented, with the club seemingly incapable of finding anyone to match the glory days under Sir Alex Ferguson.

Since his departure in 2013, they have had eight managers – seven of whom have managed them in Europe's biggest competition.

The three-time champions of Europe have performed particularly poorly in the Champions League in that time, not making it past the quarter-finals once in seven attempts.

They have won less than half of their Champions League fixtures since Ferguson left – and only 34 per cent in the current decade.

Carrick brought United back into the Champions League last season but since being given the permanent role has hit shocking form

And they will be lucky to even reach that stage this season if they continue to play as they have been in the competition, losing to Atletico Madrid away and being embarrassed by Champions League debutants Como.

With United set to take on Roma on Tuesday in their fourth game of the competition, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at how each manager on United's carousel has fared in the Champions League... and where it unravelled for all of them.

It feels as if it has been an age since David Moyes took the reins at Old Trafford. The Scotsman had a torrid time in his ten-month spell at United.

His tenure was characterised by embarrassing losses, a lack of consistency and an inability to transition from the old regime.

Moyes was sacked in April after a 2-0 loss to his old Everton side that ended United's hopes of a top-four finish for that season. He was already under serious pressure having been dumped out of the Champions League in the quarter-finals by Bayern Munich.

Moyes was handpicked by Ferguson to replace him but didn't even last a season at United

The current Everton manager oversaw a 1-1 draw at home in the first leg, with Nemanja Vidic's goal being cancelled out by Bastian Schweinsteiger – who moved to Old Trafford a year later. But Bayern – managed by Pep Guardiola – quickly responded to Patrice Evra's goal in the second leg to win it 3-1.

They had to battle to even get that far, with a comfortable group stage – four wins and two draws – being followed by an embarrassing 2-0 defeat at Olympiacos in the first leg of the last 16. A Robin van Persie hat-trick in the second leg spared their blushes.

The big Dutchman came to United with a stellar CV having won both the Champions League and UEFA Cup with Ajax in the 90s, as well as league titles in Spain and Germany.

And he seemed the exact kind of serial winner who would be the perfect replacement for Ferguson, but it just didn't work out. Van Gaal spent heavily in the market when he arrived - most notably breaking the British transfer record to secure the services of Angel Di Maria for £59.7million - but he simply couldn't find his feet in England.

Van Gaal had just the one season in the Champions League with United before leaving, and it was possibly the most disastrous since Ferguson's departure.

They were placed in a group with Wolfsburg, PSV and CSKA Moscow, and were dumped out at the earliest possible stage, finishing third in the group with just eight points. They fell into the Europa League and - after overturning a disastrous 2-1 defeat by Danish side Midtjylland in the first leg of their last-32 game - were sent packing by Liverpool.

Joining in 2016 after being sacked by Chelsea, Jose Mourinho immediately got busy in the market.

And initially it seemed as if he was going to make it work. Paul Pogba and Zlatan Ibrahimovic arrived and United won their first three games. Although their league form dipped, they did go on to win the League Cup and the Europa League in that first season.

But then it all began to fall away. Like Van Gaal and Moyes before him, Mourinho only got one try at his favourite competition with United, and exited in a less than graceful manner.

Jose won the Europa League whilst in Manchester but never really found success in the big competition

He may have won it with Porto in 2004 and Inter six years later but at United he only got as far as the round of 16, and crashed out after a 2-1 home defeat by Sevilla following a 0-0 draw in the first leg.

Recently Jose revealed that his relationship with the Red Devils was very nearly different. In his new Netflix biopic, Mourinho, he said that he had agreed to take over straight after Ferguson - only to be lured back to Chelsea by Roman Abramovich instead. Who knows how he would have fared at Old Trafford if he had joined three years earlier.

Mourinho's successor also had an excellent start to life in the United dugout but ended up being hounded out after a tumultuous three years.

When Ole was at the wheel, at first it seemed like United were on course to return to the big time however, slowly but surely, it became clear that it wasn't going to work out.

Solskjaer is one of two men on this list to have won the Champions League with United as a player and the Norwegian scored arguably the most historic goal in United's European history, getting the dramatic winner in the 1999 final.

And he is probably the only gaffer since Ferguson to have had a positive memorable moment in the competition. It came in Paris in March of 2019, shortly after he took over. After losing 2-0 at home in the first leg of the tie they looked like they were already out but miraculously Ole masterminded a 3-1 victory and won on away goals.

Unfortunately that is where the good times as a manager in the Champions League end. After the PSG win United were beaten 4-0 on aggregate by Barcelona and then didn't make it into the competition for the 2019-20 season.

They did return with Ole in 2020-21 - only to be knocked out in the group stage, finishing third in a group with PSG, RB Leipzig and Turkish side Basaksehir. They went on to reach the Europa League final that year - losing to Villarreal on penalties - and Solskjaer was gone in November, before the end of next season's group stage.

Taking over as interim manager until the end of the 2021-22 campaign - following a caretaker spell from a certain Michael Carrick - Austrian Rangnick was in charge for just three European games.

The final game of the group stage saw a 1-1 draw with Swiss side Young Boys, with Mason Greenwood scoring United's goal.

Then they took on Atletico Madrid in the last-16, and after a 1-1 draw away, were sent packing with a 1-0 second-leg defeat at Old Trafford.

Renan Lodi's header for Atletico Madrid sent United crashing out under Ralf Rangnick

Rangnick's spell at United is best remembered for his forthright assessments of the club's dire situation, and he famously likened their situation to that of a patient needing open-heart surgery.

'You don’t even need glasses to see and analyse where the problems are,' he said. 'Now it’s about how do we solve them? It’s not enough to do some minor amendments. In medicine you would say that this is an operation of the open heart.

'If this happens and everyone has realised that this has to happen and if people want to work together then it makes sense and I believe it doesn’t take two or three years to change those things. This can happen within one year.'

More than four years on, the fans are still waiting.

Erik ten Hag came in nine years after Ferguson's exit, and while he brought a League Cup and an FA Cup to Old Trafford it was not enough to stop him being sacked.

Like Van Gaal and Solskjaer, Ten Hag's United failed to make it past the group stage of the Champions League. He actually fared even worse than his predecessors by finishing rock bottom of the group in the 2023-24 season, after particularly rough losses away to Copenhagen and Galatasaray.

Like Van Gaal and Solskjaer, Ten Hag's United failed to make it past the group stage of the Champions League

After a dismal eighth-placed finish in the Premier League the FA Cup win over Manchester City ended that season on a high - and saved Ten Hag's job.

He even signed a contract extension that summer, but was ditched by October with United 14th.

Ruben Amorim, who replaced Ten Hag, did not manage United in the Champions League - though he did reach the Europa League final with them in 2025.

His sacking in January this year paved the way for Michael Carrick to join as interim and, in steering them to third place, ensured United were back at Europe's top table after two seasons away.

That also won him the permanent role, but Carrick has had a torrid start to the new campaign - winning just two of his side's 13 games in all competitions and setting a new club record for the longest winless streak in the Premier League era (nine).

One of those wins was in the Champions League against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah, but they followed that with the defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como.

Carrick will hope United can finally arrest this run of form at home to Roma on Tuesday, but it will not be easy with the Italians enjoying an excellent start to the season and currently sitting third in Serie A.

A win, however, could keep Carrick in a job and breathe some life into a United team that desperately needs it.

#1880. ‘Ridiculous threat’ – Xabi Alonso told that ex-Liverpool star would ‘thrive’ at Chelsea

Alan Hutton believes that Trent Alexander-Arnold would ‘thrive’ if he reunited with former Real Madrid boss Xabi Alonso at Chelsea.

Alexander-Arnold left his boyhood club Liverpool to join the Spanish giants two summers ago, but injuries saw him feature just 21 times in the league under Alonso and his interim replacement, Alvaro Arbeloa.

While fit this campaign, the Englishman has still struggled for regular minutes under Jose Mourinho and has started just one of Real’s last six matches in all competitions.

Summer signing Denzel Dumfries has moved above Alexander-Arnold in the pecking order, while Mourinho has also deployed Federico Valverde as a makeshift right-back over the Englishman.

Given that lack of game time, Hutton believes that Alexander-Arnold may soon start to consider his options.

And the former Premier League full-back earmarked Chelsea as the perfect club to get the 28-year-old back to his best.

‘Trent Alexander-Arnold could thrive at Chelsea because Xabi Alonso would use him in the correct manner and get the best out of him, because his attacking threat is ridiculous,’ Hutton told OLBG.

‘What he sees, his vision, his passing ability, it’s right up there.

‘It is strange when you watch Real Madrid, I was watching El Clásico and Valverde played at right-back while Dumfries and Trent were on the bench.

‘Even for me, as good a player as Valverde is, he’s a midfielder, so that would hurt you a bit. It’s been a shame that it hasn’t quite worked out, but he’s so talented.

‘I think a move back to the Premier League would suit him, he knows it inside out. Someone like Alonso, with what he’d want from him, would use him in the correct manner and get the best out of him.’

Speaking recently, Mourinho admitted that omitting Alexander-Arnold has been a painful decision.

‘First of all, it hurts me. I don’t like to make players feel bad. I want them to feel good,’ Mourinho said.

‘Obviously, when you build a squad with two players per position as your foundation and then have a third player take the field, that’s something I don’t like.

‘But there are things that are more important than these feelings. Things that are more important for the team at a given moment. And I decided that right now, the move was to change up the midfield and put Fede [Valverde] in there.’

And with speculation likely to mount ahead of the January transfer window, former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said he would welcome Alexander-Arnold back to Anfield.

‘I’d have him back,’ Carragher said on The Overlap. ‘He would get a lot of criticism, because I think he made a mistake. I think he made a big mistake going to Madrid.

‘We’ve definitely missed his creativity.’

#1879. Leeds United v Tottenham Hotspur: Daniel Farke on 'elite' duo on opposing sides at Elland Road

Something else sets them apart from their contemporaries.

It was brought into sharp focus by Harry Kane's recent elevation to Ballon d'Or winner amid a glittering ceremony in his home city of London.

Kane's staggering goalscoring numbers and consistency speaks for itself, but it hardly happened overnight.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

What sets him apart is his elite mentality from an early age. 'Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise' was his social media post after being named as the best footballer in the world.

For all his trappings and status, no one could ever describe him as narcissistic.

That message might just resonate with two players on opposing sides today: Archie Gray and James Trafford.

The former, of course, is well known to Leeds United supporters. In an ideal world, he will still be stepping out in the white of Leeds and not Tottenham Hotspur.

It's hard to believe that Gray is still not yet 21 - that milestone arrives in March.

He is part-way through his third season in the Premier League and fourth campaign as a first-teamer. He is not far shy of 150 competitive games already in a career which is surely only going one way.

Capable of playing centre-back, full-back and midfield, he is a manager's dream. Tactically adept, responsible and mature beyond his years, it's easy to see that he belongs to a revered football dynasty.

He is also driven, football-obsessed and low-maintenance. The sort of person - and not just player - that Daniel Farke likes. Even if he will not be wanting to see any of his acumen today.

Farke said: "It was early to see (his elite mentality). When Archie came through at the age of 17, he replaced my vice-captain and our club legend Luke Ayling.

"It was not an easy decision. It was not for the dressing room. I came in as the new coach and I've got a club legend. Together with Liam Cooper, he was wearing the captain's armband.

"But he was on the bench because I played Archie, a 17-year-old kid. But Archie had already at this age more or less this mentality and the quality. He was a different drawer (top-drawer).

"The same when I played him in midfield - you had experienced players like Glen Kamara, for example, out for his position. But just due to the quality and mentality that (Gray) he had meant he was ready and prepared to play on a Championship level.

"I think he has also sometimes worn the captain's armband for Tottenham at a more prominent level.

"It says a lot about him and you need this quality and mentality if you want to be there as a young player playing so many games on this level."

As with Kane, Gray has had to handle knockbacks - being part of a Spurs side that has flirted with relegation in the past few seasons. It's something that Leeds and England goalkeeper Trafford also knows a fair bit about.

The 24-year-old heads into the game on the back of a howler in last weekend's loss to Bournemouth - gifting a goal to Cherries player Evanilson.

He was also culpable—though by no means as damningly - for Riccardo Calafiori's goal in United's 2-1 reverse at Arsenal on October 10.

Mistakes are - and will forever remain - an omnipresent part of a goalkeeper's life.

Trafford also currently has the best save percentage in the Premier League at 80.5. Only Hull City's Konstantinos Tzolakis - with 32 saves - has stopped more shots so far this term.

So the Cumbrian, from a humble farming roots near Cockermouth, has plenty to shout about if he cares to. Which he doesn't.

Farke said: "He's really top. James has delivered top performances for us so far.

"He was, of course, involved in the first goal (at Bournemouth) and sadly in this case it was then decisive, but that's also what you have to deal with, especially as a young player and young goalkeeper.

"You deal with these setbacks and learn from them and it's quite important for me that he didn't look shy of confidence during this week.

"He was there with his normal performance. I'm pretty sure he has also learned from it, but for me it's also important that he doesn't lose his confidence and his rhythm. Of course, he will be in goal and also hopefully with an important display."

Speaking of statistics, Leeds head into the game in receipt of an unwanted Premier League record: they have not won a top-flight game played before 3pm on a Saturday in 21 attempts since March 2022.

Ending that statistic would be a nice way to head into an international break, not that Farke is losing any sleep over it.

"I wouldn't take too much into the timing', the German opined.

"I think it's also normal. In the last years we were on Premier League level, we've spent more or less all the time in the relegation pattern, so it's less likely to win games in comparison to Man City or Liverpool or Arsenal right now. It's another chance to break the record, it's important to be switched on."

#1878. Marcus Rashford names player closest to Lionel Messi's level

By Naim Beneddra | 06 Nov 2026 16:57

Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has named Lamine Yamal as the most talented footballer he has played alongside, suggesting that the Barcelona teenager could eventually come close to matching Lionel Messi's extraordinary achievements.

The England international spent the 2025-26 campaign on loan at Barcelona, where he developed a close appreciation of Yamal's abilities before returning to Old Trafford during the summer.

Despite having shared a dressing room with some of football's biggest names, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Harry Kane, Rashford believes the 19-year-old possesses a level of natural talent unlike anything he has previously encountered.

Speaking during a question-and-answer session with Manchester United supporters at Old Trafford, the 29-year-old revealed that he had personally told Yamal how highly he rated him before leaving Barcelona.

Rashford went even further by suggesting that the Spanish international could end his career with seven Ballon d'Or awards, an achievement that would place him within touching distance of Messi's record.

Rashford's comments came during an appearance in Manchester United's Ambassadors' Lounge ahead of Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Roma.

The forward, who has been sidelined by injury in recent weeks, was asked about Messi and the prospects of his former Barcelona teammate following the recent Ballon d'Or ceremony.

He explained that he had already spoken directly to Yamal about his abilities before completing his return to Manchester.

"Before I left Barcelona, I told him I'd played with some very talented players, but he was above them all," Rashford said, in comments reported by the Manchester Evening News.

The former Aston Villa loanee was particularly struck by how much Yamal had achieved despite still being a teenager.

"I've never seen a player at that age be as talented as he is," he continued.

"For me, he's the closest somebody can get to the level of Messi over the years."

The comparison carries considerable weight given Rashford's experience at the highest level.

He played alongside Ronaldo during the Portuguese star's second spell at Manchester United and has also shared the pitch with Kane for England.

However, Rashford's assessment was focused on Yamal's exceptional ability at such a young age, rather than suggesting that the Barcelona winger has already surpassed those established stars in terms of career achievements.

The United attacker also made clear that he still considers Messi an almost impossible standard to replicate.

Describing the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner as a complete footballing genius, Rashford acknowledged that another player with the Argentine's full range of abilities may never emerge.

Nevertheless, his admiration for Yamal's potential was unmistakable.

The England international believes the Barcelona youngster possesses the talent to remain among the world's leading players for many years, provided he continues developing at his current rate.

Rashford's prediction about Yamal's future went beyond comparing his playing style and natural ability with Messi.

The Manchester United forward suggested that the teenager could eventually collect seven Ballon d'Or trophies.

"If he goes on to win seven Ballons d'Or, I wouldn't be surprised," Rashford explained.

It was a remarkable assessment of a player who has yet to win the senior award but has already finished among its leading contenders on three occasions.

Yamal placed eighth in 2024, finished runner-up to Ousmane Dembele in 2025 and took third place in October's 2026 ceremony, behind winner Harry Kane and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe.

He also collected his third consecutive Kopa Trophy last month, having won the award for the world's best young player in 2024 and 2025.

The Barcelona star's rapid rise has been accompanied by major collective success.

He played a central role in Spain's Euro 2024 triumph before helping his country win the 2026 World Cup, while also establishing himself as one of the most influential players in Hansi Flick's Barcelona side.

At club level, Yamal has already become a regular match-winner, combining exceptional dribbling ability with increasingly productive contributions in front of goal.

Rashford also took the opportunity to congratulate Kane on his Ballon d'Or success, revealing that he had sent the Bayern Munich striker a personal message after the ceremony.

The United forward felt that Kane's outstanding goalscoring record and creative output made him a deserving winner of the prestigious award.

His support for Kane did not diminish his enthusiasm about Yamal's future, with Rashford clearly viewing the Spaniard's best years as still to come.

For Rashford himself, the comments offer an insight into the lasting impression left by his season in Catalonia.

Barcelona declined to activate the purchase option in his loan agreement, leading to his return to Manchester United, where he is attempting to revive his career under Michael Carrick.

His admiration for Yamal, however, has evidently remained undiminished.

Having witnessed the teenager's qualities at close quarters, Rashford believes the Barcelona number 10 has the potential to build a career that invites comparisons with the greatest players the sport has produced.
